INTRODUCTION

This policy details the guidelines and regulations related to the car benefits as applicable under the relevant scheme (Company-Owned Car Scheme or Employee-Owned Car Scheme).
This policy ensures that employees understand their responsibilities and obligations when availing of the car benefits.

1.1 Policy Management

Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Compensation & Benefits Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

Policy Amendments and Updates
The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.2 Responsibilities, Compliance

The car policy aims to protect the company's vehicles (Cars) and other assets. It establishes guidelines for the proper use, maintenance, and care of company-owned Cars.
The car policy ensures that employees comply with all applicable laws and regulations related to Car use.

Company Car Policy (CCP) for Group Executive Committee (“GEC”)

Scope
This section of the policy is applicable to all the employees who are part of Group Executive Committee for Meridian Finance (Meridian Finance).

Policy Details: CCP for GEC
Registration

The Car will be purchased and registered in the name of the Company on the basis of eligibility of respective GEC member.

Type of Cars:
Petrol Cars, Diesel Cars, Dual Fuel Cars (Petrol/CNG or Diesel/CNG), Electronic Vehicle (EV) including Sports Utility Vehicles (SUVs) and Multi-Utility Vehicles (MUVs) are permitted under CCP.
Eligibility period for taking a New Car under CCP for GEC.

A GEC member will be eligible to purchase a new car post completion of 48 months from the date of delivery of the previous Car.

Limits:
SL Grade: Rs 40,00,000 (excluding taxes).
EL and BL Grade: Rs 35,00,000 (excluding taxes).
Reimbursements:

Insurance Charges and Maintenance expenses will be borne by the Company on actuals.
Fuel expenses and Driver’s Salary will be reimbursed as stated in Annexure 4.
From 2nd year onwards, the Insurance premium will be paid by the company and the amount will be recovered in the subsequent month’s payroll from the employee.

Settlement
On completion of 48 months as per CCP:
All eligible employees who avail CCP will be given a choice to purchase the car at Written Down Value (WDV) in the books of the Company.
Advance intimation will be provided to the employee 60 days prior to the expiry of CCP period to the concerned employee. The concerned employee will have to confirm his/her choice well before the expiry of CCP period in response to the advance intimation.
The written down value in the books is arrived at after providing for depreciation as per the policy followed by the Company.
Depreciation is to be calculated based on the Straight-Line method.
Depreciation to be calculated till the month prior to the sale.
The rate of depreciation would be as per the policy followed by the Company, which presently is 25% p.a. Depreciation is applied on purchase cost, as reduced by residual value.
The Residual value is calculated at the rate of 5% of the purchase cost capitalized in the books.
The transfer of car by the Company to the Employee will be treated as “Perquisite" in the hands of the Employee, which is taxable as salary under the prevailing Income-tax laws. The tax, if any, will be borne by the employee. Refer Annexure 1 for the applicable rules for Perquisite Valuation as per Income Tax Act 1961.
Other Government Taxes (presently GST, RTO transfer and other related charges) at the time of CCP settlement will be borne by the Employee. GST, if any, will be levied as per the applicable rules. Please refer Annexure 1 for the same.
If the concerned employee does not opt to buy the car as per the above option and opts to continue to use the same, then the company shall continue to bear the fuel and maintenance cost as per the eligibility. Further, the company shall also bear the cost of insurance of the said car after the CCP period of 48 months till the car continues to be in the name of the company.
If the GEC member post settlement of the CCP as above, does not opt to avail the CCP again, then the following will be available:
Fuel expenses and maintenance charges will be reimbursed as per eligibility.
The insurance of the car will be borne by the employees.
On successful closure of the current period of settlement the concerned employee would be eligible to re-enter the CCP scheme as the eligibility mentioned in the scheme.
On Resignation/Pre-closure:
The company shall seek 3 best market quotes from the used car vendors.
The employee will be offered to purchase the car at a value nominally (INR 5,000/-) higher than the H1 (highest quote) market quote.
Transfer charges and applicable taxes i.e., GST and Income tax on perquisite value, if any, will be borne by the employee.
The car will be transferred in the name of the employee.
Insurance cost will be borne by the Company upto the date of transfer of the car.
If the employee does not opt to buy the car, then the car will be sold as per the prevailing asset disposal policy of the company.
Accident, Theft of Car, Total / Partial Damage of Car due to Natural Calamity:

The insurance amount received from the Insurance Company will be credited to the Company.
Disposal of the car and the salvage value will be taken into Company’s account against the WDV of the Car.
Any loss to the Company on account of the difference between the Insurance amount / salvage value and the WDV will have to be borne by the employee.
Employee will be eligible for re-entry into this scheme immediately.
Death of an Employee
The company shall seek 3 best market quotes from the used car vendors.
The legal heirs/legal representatives of the Employee will be offered to purchase the car at a value nominally (INR 5,000) higher than the H1 (highest quote) market quote.
Transfer charges and applicable taxes i.e., GST and Income tax on perquisite value, if any, will be borne by the legal heir/ legal representative.
The Car will be transferred to the legal heirs/ legal representatives of the deceased employee.
Insurance cost will be borne by the company upto the date of transfer of the car.
If the legal heirs/legal representatives of deceased employees decline the option to purchase the car, then the said car will be sold as per the prevailing asset disposal policy of the company.

Company Owned Car Scheme (“COCS”):

Scope

This section of the policy has been formulated to provide guidelines for Motor-car related facilities for Employees in the grade OL I & above for official duties.
This section of the policy is applicable to all the employees of Grade OL I & above of Meridian Finance (Meridian Finance) other than GEC.
This does not include the fuel reimbursement forming part of the Local travel and Out station travel.

Policy Details: COCS
Registration

The Car will be purchased (only brand-new car from authorized dealers) and registered in the name of the Company on the basis of eligibility of respective employees of Band OL I & Above.

Type of Cars:
Petrol Cars, Diesel Cars, Dual Fuel Cars (Petrol/CNG or Diesel/CNG), Electronic Vehicle (EV) are permitted under the COCS.
Period of COCS:
Such facility will be spread across 48 months (4 years)
CTC of employee opting for such car facility shall be suitably revised.
Cost of the Car shall comprise of Base price + Registration charges + Government taxes + Accessories + 1st year Insurance premium.

Limits:
BL Band & above: Rs 25,00,000 (Base Price excluding taxes)
OL I Grade: Rs 15,00,000 (Base Price excluding taxes) The above is maximum limits for availing the COCS.

Reimbursements:

Insurance Charges for the 1st year will be a part of the total cost which will be included as a part of monthly adjustment.
From 2nd year onwards, the Insurance premium will be paid by the company and the amount will be recovered in the subsequent month’s payroll from the employee.
Monthly Driver’s Salary, Fuel and maintenance expenses will be reimbursed on actuals from CTC of the employee subject to limits defined in Annexure 4
Employees need to provide a declaration that the expenses incurred on Fuel & Maintenance and Driver’s salary is for official duties.
Employees under COCS policy will neither be eligible for Company transport for travel within the city limits nor claim local conveyance reimbursement through vouchers nor any other conveyance allowance.
Motor-car facilities provided by the Company to the Employee will be treated as “Perquisite” in the hands of the Employee, which is taxable as Salary under the prevailing Income-tax laws. Refer Annexure 2 (in knowledge base on the HR portal) for Perquisite Value computation.
Employee to furnish proof of actual spent of such reimbursement.
Settlement:
All eligible employees who enter the scheme will have to mandatorily purchase the car at Written Down Value (WDV) in the books on completion of COCS period.
Advance intimation will be provided to the employee 1 month prior to completion of stipulated 48 months period.
The written down value (including residual value) in the books is arrived at after providing for depreciation as per the policy followed by the Company.
Depreciation is to be calculated based on the Straight-Line method.
Depreciation to be calculated till the month prior to the sale.
The rate of depreciation would be as per the policy followed by the Company, which presently is 25% p.a.
The transfer of car by the Company to the Employee will be treated as “Perquisite" in the hands of the Employee, which is taxable as salary under the prevailing Income-tax laws. The tax, if any, will be borne by the employee. Refer Annexure 3 (in knowledge base on the HR portal) for the applicable rules for Perquisite Valuation as per Income Tax Act 1961
Other Government Taxes (presently GST, RTO transfer and other related charges) at the time of COCS settlement will be borne by the Employee. GST, if any, will be levied as per the applicable rules.
In case of Resignation / Pre-Closure, employees have to purchase the car at Residual Value that will be calculated after considering depreciation till the month prior to the sale of the car.
The transfer process should be completed by the process not later than 90 days from the date of closure of 48 months period.
Re-Eligibility:
On completion of COCS Period of 48 months and settlement of Car transfer, employee will be re-eligible for the COCS scheme.

Other Settlement Scenarios under COCS:
Change of Grade of Eligible Employees:
In case, the eligible employee is promoted to a higher grade (e.g., OLI to BLIII), he/ she is entitled for higher limits of COCS. In such case, such employee can opt for a car subject to the following:
Employee needs to mandatory buy the Original Car at the WDV and pay all applicable taxes.
An approval is obtained from GEC member.
New car is purchased in accordance with the revised entitlement under COCS.
Perquisite and GST on transfer shall be borne by the employee.
Accident, Theft of Car, Total / Partial Damage of Car due to Natural Calamity:

The insurance amount received from the Insurance Company will be credited to the Company.
Disposal of the car and the salvage value will be taken into Company’s account against the WDV of the Car.
Any loss to the Company on account of the difference between the Insurance amount / salvage value and the WDV will have to be borne by the employee.
Employee will be eligible for re-entry into this scheme immediately.
Death of an Employee
The legal heirs/legal representatives of the Employee have an option to make the payment towards the WDV of the Car to the company.
Transfer Charges and applicable taxes i.e., GST and Income Tax on perquisite value, if any, will be borne by the legal heirs/ legal representatives.
The Car will be transferred to the legal heirs/ legal representatives of the deceased employee.
If the legal heirs/legal representatives of deceased employees decline the option to purchase the car at WDV, then the said car will be considered for sale in the market to the highest bidder/ kept in the company pool of cars till disposal / other eligible employees (under the COCS)
Process for Entry into COCS:
Employees send an email to the Business HR communicating the intention to avail COCS.
Employee HR forwards the request to FCM after post validating the criteria met as per COCS policy.
Employee negotiates rates and discounts with the dealers at regular intervals and informs FCM.
Employee chooses the car to be purchased within eligible limits and forwards the Dealer Proforma Invoice along with the copy of the Sanction letter to FCM Department for the release of Purchase Order (PO). Dealer Proforma Invoice (in the name of the company) should include:
GST Registration number and Pan No. of the dealer and the Company
Base Price
Registration charges (amounts payable to RTO)
Government taxes (GST)
One time service-charges, if any
Cost of accessories (Should not exceed the sanction limit)
Insurance charges (to be borne by the Company)
Corporate Discount, if any
On receipt of the above documents, the FCM raises a Purchase Order for the car and sends it to the employee.
Employees then forward the following documents to Finance Department along with the following documents:
Copy of the Sanction Letter
Purchase Order
Original Proforma Invoice
Invoice for cost of accessories
On receipt of the original documents, Finance raises the cheque in the name of the Dealer and sends it to the employee. The date of issue of cheque will be the entry date of the Car Scheme
Employee forwards the cheque to the Dealer, also inspects the car, and obtains the car details required with respect to registration of the car.
Employee forwards the car details received from FCM for insuring the car.
FCM forwards the Original Insurance Certificate to the employee and copy to the Finance.
FCM sends the following documents to the dealer for Registration in Company’s name:
Copy of Insurance Certificate
Letter to RTO
Original RTO Receipts
Final Invoice
Care Delivery details
Car undertaking duly signed, Entry date will be the date on which the company issues the cheque in the name of the dealer.
FCM forwards this detail to C&B team in HR to update.
C&B team in HR calculates the revised CTC (only Special Allowance to be changed. Other components remain unchanged) and advise HR Ops team to issue the revised letter.
Post issuance of the revised CTC letter, HR Ops makes necessary changes in the CTC to effect in payroll.
Procedure for Settlement of COCS dues:

Normal Closure after end of 4 years:
HR Ops intimates the employees 2 months in advance about the completion of the COCS period with a copy to FCM and Finance Department

Resignation before completion of 4 years:
On receipt of resignation from the employee, the Business HR intimates FCM and Finance department.

Retirement before completion of 4 years:

HR Ops to intimate FCM/Finance Department the date of superannuation of the employee well in advance.

3.5.4 General Guidelines for Settlement of COCS dues:
In case of Normal Closure, Employees should initiate the car transfer formalities in advance and transfer the car to own name before approaching HR for a car sanction.
The employees to submit Form No 28, 29 and 30 to Transportation Department along with address proof (Aadhaar/ Passport/ LIC policy/ Election Card). Employee submits these forms to the Transportation Department within 15 days of COCS closure. Transportation Department checks whether all the documents are in order and submits them to the RTO. The RTO submits to CID for verification. Transport Department receives the receipt of documents from the RTO and sends a copy to the employee. If the documents are in order, the Transport Department received the receipt of documents within 45 days, otherwise it takes longer.
Finance department calculates the Residual value of the car and intimates to the employee through FCM/HR Ops team.
Employees can make the payment of the Residual Value of the car to the Finance department.
FCM sends an intimation to the employee along with necessary documents for transfer of the car. The transfer charges will be borne by the employee.
FCM department issues Delivery notes only after Transport Department gives clearance.
On completion of the Transfer process, the Original Registration certificate (Smart Card) is sent by RTO to the employee’s residence. Employee sends copy of the Registration certificate to the FCM and HR Ops team.
On confirmation by FCM of asset removal, Finance passes appropriate entries for removal of assets from the Books of Accounts.

Employee-owned Car Scheme (“EOCS”)
Scope

This section of the policy has been formulated to provide guidelines for Motor-car related facilities for all Employees owning a car and using it for official purpose apart from personal use.
This policy is applicable to all the employees of Meridian Finance (Meridian Finance) other than GEC.
This policy does not include the fuel reimbursement forming part of Local travel and Outstation travel policy in HR Manual.

Policy Details: EOCS
General Guidelines
All employees (other than GEC) are eligible to claim Reimbursement of Fuel & Maintenance and Driver’s Salary for motorcar owned by the employees and used for official purpose.
Currently, this will be applicable for FL/SB grades and above...
Employees can apply for entry into EOCS by updating Flexi Compensation option in SSC module along with a copy of the Registration Certificate showing ownership of car in their name.
Reimbursements
Monthly Driver’s Salary, Fuel and maintenance expenses will be reimbursed on actuals from CTC of the employee.
Employees opting for reimbursement will neither be eligible for Company transport within local city limits nor claim local conveyance reimbursement through vouchers.
The above reimbursement facilities provided by the Company to the Employee will be treated as “Perquisite” in the hands of the Employee, which is taxable as Salary under the prevailing Income-tax laws. Refer Annexure 1 (in knowledge base on the HR portal) for Perquisite Value computation.
HR Operations to validate and confirm that such employee is eligible to claim monthly reimbursement.
Employees need to furnish proof of actual spent of such reimbursement along with declaration that such expenditure is incurred for official duties.

EMPLOYEE SEPARATION AND FINAL SETTLEMENT POLICY

Policy Title
| Employee Separation and Final Settlement Policy
|
Applicability
| Applicable to all full-time employees of Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.
|
Coverage
| Employee Separation
Final Settlement Guidelines
|
Prepared by
| Team, Compensation & Benefits
|
Reviewed By
| Head - Compensation & Benefits
|
Approved By
| Chief Human Resources Officer

|
Effective date
|
|

The Employee Separation and Final Settlement Policy is designed to provide a structured and transparent process for managing the departure of employees from our organization.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy manual should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that all policies and processes stipulated in this version shall supersede those set out in any earlier versions of the HR manual. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required. Notwithstanding, Meridian Finance will follow the prevailing statutory requirements at the point of any application / notification.

INTRODUCTION

Employees may be separated from the organization due to various reasons, including:
Resignation (Voluntary Exit): Employees have the option to resign from their position, demonstrating their commitment to providing adequate notice.
Involuntary Resignation (Asked to leave): Employees are asked by the company to leave due to misconduct, disciplinary issue, non-performance, change in the organization structure or any other reasons as elaborated in this document further.
Termination: The procedure in which an employee's employment is ended by the employer rather than the employee is known as an involuntary termination.
Absconding: The act of leaving a job or a situation without permission or notification, often with the intention of avoiding responsibility or consequences.
Death: This is a situation where the employment comes to an end due to an unfortunate demise of the employee.
Retirement and Superannuation: Employees have the opportunity to retire either at the normal retirement age i.e. 58 years or 60 years as determined by the company.
By following this policy, Meridian Finance strives to maintain positive relationships with departing employees and uphold our commitment to fair and equitable treatment.

1.1 Policy Objective

The purpose of this policy is to outline the procedures and guidelines for managing the employee separation process and final settlement. It aims to facilitate a smooth transition for both the departing employee and the organization, while ensuring that all legal and financial obligations are met.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Compensation & Benefits Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates
The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The Exit process is processed by the BHR and HR Ops Team. The below matrix provides detail on the roles and responsibilities of the different stakeholders involved in the exit process.

Type of exits
| Raised/Initiated
| Approval
|
Voluntary Resignation
| Employee
| BHR
|
Involuntary Resignation
| BHR
| BHR
|
Termination
| HR Operations
| HR Operations
|
Absconding
| HR Operations
| HR Operations
|
Death
| HR Operations
| HR Operations
|
Retirement
| BHR
| BHR
|

HR Operations team have access to modify the last working date in the HR portal as per the request received from BHRs.

Notice Period
Policy Guidelines

The notice period is defined based on the Employee Job Bands and the nature of their job functions.
Notice shortfall is recovered from the full & final settlement. The last drawn basic salary shall be applicable for recovery. Adjustment of leave balances against notice period is not permitted.
Settlement of leaves balances against notice period is permitted only at the discretion of the management.
Employee shall receive his/her Full & Final settlement within 45 working days.
Relieving & experience letter will be sent to the employee along with the full & final settlement.
No salary is credited to the employee during suspension period.

Duration of Notice period
Employee Category
| Duration of Notice period
|
FL IV other than branch operation manager
| 1 month
|
Branch Operation Manager
| 3 months
|
FL III & above
| 3 months
|
Early Release during Notice Period

In case when employee initiates early release:
Employee shall pay for the balancing period in case of early release. The amount will be calculated on Basic Pay
In case of notice period waiver, approval needs to be granted from the CHRO

In case when employer initiates early release:
Employer shall pay for the balancing period in case of early release.

Exits based on Appraisal Ratings

Employees who obtain a rating as 1 are asked to leave the organization
Employees who obtain a rating as 2 are given performance improvement plan (3 months)
Performs: Employee is retained
Unable to perform: Employee is asked to leave
Resignation (Voluntary Exits)
Scope

This policy applies to all employees who voluntarily resign from their employment with the organization.

Timeline & Responsibilities

The BHR is responsible to update the last date of working.
The resignation needs to be accepted by manager and BHR before employee completes the notice period.
The exit interview takes place within 48 hours of resignation.

Step by Step Process

Step 1, Employee to fill the exit form mandatorily and then submit resignation.
Step 2 - BHRs will get mail communication when employee submits the exit form.
Step 3 - BHR will conduct exit interview within 48 hours of resignation.
Step 4, Post Interview
If Employee agrees to stay in the organization, then the employee will be asked to revoke the resignation from the system.
If the employee is continuing with the resignation, then they shall be directed to serve the notice period as per the duration mentioned in Clause 2.2

Involuntary Resignation (Asked to Leave - ATL)
Scope

This policy applies to all employees, where the organization formally requests an employee to leave their position. The employees are not required to serve notice period in most such cases.

Conditions of ATL:

Behavioural/Disciplinary issues
Behavioral issues: Refers to any pattern of behaviour exhibited by an employee that deviates from the expected norms or standards of conduct. This can include actions such as insubordination, disruptive behaviour, harassment, or conflicts with colleagues.
Disciplinary issues: Arises when an employee's behaviour violates company policies, codes of conduct, or legal regulations.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the Manager or BHR or employee
Integrity Issues
Cash misappropriation: Refers to the unlawful or unauthorized taking, manipulation, or misuse of cash funds belonging to the company. This can involve actions such as theft, embezzlement, or fraudulent financial transactions.
Supervisory lapse: Occurs when those in supervisory positions neglect their responsibilities or fail to adequately monitor and address issues within their purview.
Process lapse: refers to a breakdown or failure in the established procedures or workflows designed to achieve specific objectives or outcomes.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the RCU team.
Non-Performance

RAG (Red, Amber, Green) action: Employees who fall within the "red zone" are placed on a PIP and if they continue to be a non-performer then they are Asked to Leave.
PIP based exit: If the employee continues to be a non-performer after PIP, then he/she is Asked to Leave.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the Manager or BHR.
Negative Background Verification (BGV)
Red report: refers to a report or document that highlights significant concerns or discrepancies identified during the background screening process. Eg - discrepancies in employment history, education credentials, criminal records etc.
Dual employment: refers to a situation where an employee holds two or more jobs simultaneously, either within the same company or with different employers.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the RCU team or BHR.
Organization Related
Rightsizing: refers to the process of adjusting the workforce to an optimal size to improve efficiency, productivity, and financial health.
Closure of business: Refers to the closure of any branch or location of the business.
Restructuring: Restructuring in an organization refers to the comprehensive process of reorganizing the company's structure, operations, or finances.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the BHR.
Code of Conduct (COC) violation
A COC violation in an organization occurs when an employee or representative fails to follow the ethical guidelines, policies, and behaviour standards set by the company.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the RCU team
Discontinuation of contract
Such a situation occurs when the contract with the employee is discontinued.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the BHR.
End of Contract
Such a situation occurs when the employment contract with the employee is not extended or renewed.
In such cases the ATL is initiated by the HR
Stakeholders Involved
In case of Ask to Leave situation, the separation is initiated by Manager, HR or by the RCU team under various circumstances as mentioned above in clause 4.2. However, there are also other committees whose involvement is important to assess the situation. The investigating committees involved are:
POSH Committee
Code of Conduct Committee

Step by Step Process

Step 1 - BHRs to receive the communication mail regarding ATL recommendation.
Step 2, BHRs to evaluate the request in hand.
Step 3, BHR to take the following action based on the ATL request received.
When a severe offense occurs, an investigation is conducted (Employee may be suspended during this period).
Closing the case with a formal warning letter.
Closing the case with a soft warning (if no further action is taken).
Employee is informed of ATL process.
Step 4, When a severe offense occurs, an investigation is conducted, Respective investigation team investigate the case.
Post investigation if any major find outs have been concluded, then the BHR may either issue a warning to the employee or initiate employee separation.
Step 5 - When Employee is informed of ATL process by BHR, If the employee disagrees, then an investigation shall take place and the conclusions of the investigation will be presented to BHR and CHRO for approval.
The approval is shared with HR Ops team to prepare for the termination letter.
Respective HR Team will be issuing the termination letter and confirm the further steps to HR Ops team for further process.
If the employee agrees with the ATL process, then the employee will fill the exit form and then submit resignation on the HR portal.
BHRs will get mail communication when employee submits the exit form.
Immediate supervisor and BHRs to accept the resignation.
Employee either get immediate release or they have to serve specific notice periods depending on the severity of the case.
Termination
Scope
The procedure in which an employee's employment is ended by the employer rather than the employee is known as an involuntary termination.
This type of exit is initiated by the organization for various reasons and follows a structured approach to ensure fairness, compliance, and minimal disruption.
Employees are Terminated only when the situation is very serious and not in line with the company's rules and standards.
Conditions of Termination
When an employee violates the code of conduct which comes under zero-tolerance zone.
Data Breaching case
Theft case
POSH case
Being violent at work case
Others
Step by Step Process
Step 1 - BHRs to receive the communication mail regarding termination of an employee.
Step 2, Investigated concluded case with recommendation of termination to be presented to respective BHR & CHRO for an approval.
Step 3, HR Ops Team will receive the approval and then make the termination letter for employee.
Step 4 - Respective HR team to issue termination letter and confirm the same with HR Ops Team for further process.
Absconding
Scope and Conditions for Absconding

It is termed as an unauthorized absence of an employee from duty for a continuous period of 5 days without informing their immediate supervisor.
On 6th day the employee will be termed as “Abscond” by the manager.
Step by Step Process

Step 1, During the 5 days of employee’s absence, Manager and BHRs will send communication mail to employee to check on the employee return to office.
Step 2, On 6th day the Manager or BHR to Establish communication to find out the reason behind the employee’s absence from office and take further action accordingly.
Step 3 - BHRs to contact the employee to understand the reason for their absence and accepts the request by the manager.
Step 4 - HR Ops Team to issue warning letter to the employee via email and in hard copy, requesting their return to the office within the next 5 days.
Step 5, If the employee returns back to the office, then no further steps will be taken.
Step 6, If the employee does not return to the office, then the system will automatically mark the employee as “Absconded”. The HR Ops team to mark the status of the employee as inactive in the system.
Death
Scope and Timelines
An exit process where the organization follows the procedure when the employee passes away during the service period.
The last working day of employee is the day he passes away.
Ex-Gracia (Discretionary by organization)
A sum of 2 lakhs is provided to the family as below:
If the employee was married: the amount is given to spouse.
If the employee was unmarried: the amount is given to parents.
The education of two children, up to and including graduation, is fully sponsored.
The education of an employee's spouse, till and including graduation, is sponsored (as per the limit defined). Additionally, based on merit, the spouse is eligible to interview for positions within the organization.
The Monthly salary for 2 years is provided to the family:
If the employee was married: the amount is given to spouse.
If the employee was unmarried: the amount is given to parents.
Step by Step Process
Step 1, BHRs to send an email to the HR Operations Team informing them of the employee's passing.
Step 2, HR Ops Team to update the passing away date of employee as their last working date in the the HR portal.
Step 3 - BHRs to send the documents of employee’s detail to HR Ops Team.
Step 4, Benefits to be provided to the employee’s family are as below:
The Group term life insurance amount is to be paid to the nominee of the deceased employee.
The Gratuity amount to be paid to the nominee of the deceased employee.
The PF maturity amount is to be paid to the spouse (if deceased employee was married) or parents (if deceased employee was single).
The maturity amount from EDLI will be paid to the employee’s dependents.

Retirement
Eligibility

All employees (except Executive Director / Managing Director) of Meridian Finance, on attainment of age of 58 years, shall be deemed to be retired from the Company. Executive Director / Managing Director shall retire at the age of 60 years from the Company.
Such employees and Executive Director/Managing Director shall retire on the last working day of the month in which they complete 58 years and 60 years of age respectively.
The accrued privilege leave, if any, shall be encashed on retirement after deducting any utilized prorated PL for the current year.

Step by Step Process:

Step 1, BHRs will receive a list of employees scheduled to retire within the next six months.
Step 2, BHRs will talk to the managers of the employees if they need to fill that position.
Step 3, If the Managers are not able to fill the position internally, then the recruitment process shall be initiated for the position.
Step 4, Retired employees are honored with a formal farewell gathering.
Step 5 - The status of employee retirements is updated on the HR portal by the BHRs.

Full and Final (F&F) Settlement Procedure
Roles and Responsibilities
Full & Final settlement is processed by HR Operation on the basis of clearance inputs received from all stakeholders.
Stakeholders involved in this process are:
HR Operations,
Business HR,
Central Operations,
Finance,
Information Technology,
FCM,
Shared Service Centre (SSC).

The below matrix provides detail on the roles and responsibilities of the different stakeholders involved in the F&F process.

Type of exits
| Raised/Initiated
| Approval
|
Voluntary Resignation
| Employee
| BHR
|
Involuntary Resignation
| BHR
| BHR
|
Termination
| HR Operations
| HR Operations
|
Absconding
| HR Operations
| HR Operations
|
Death
| HR Operations
| HR Operations
|
Retirement
| BHR
| BHR
|

General Guidelines

Joining bonus, BYOD and any other recoverable shall be as per the terms agreed upon in offer letter.
Leave encashment is payable only for employees who have completed 1 year of service. The last drawn basic salary shall be applicable for encashment.
Last working month’s salary will be kept on hold and paid along with full & final settlement.
Gratuity will be paid as per eligibility of Payment of Gratuity Act.
Any other payment/recovery, as approved, will be done in full & final settlement.

Clearence & Sign-Off
Clearance formalities completion is the first stage of Full & Final settlement process. Following are the respective departments which provide their inputs for each employee.

HR Operations team consolidates these inputs and processes it for final settlement payment.

Action items
| Stakeholders Involved
|
Notice shortfall recovery or waiver inputs

| BHR for respective platforms
|
Recovery amount for o/s advances if any.
| Accounts SPCO & Finance

|
Sign-off post reconciliation of receipt books or any other point
| Central operations SPOC

|
Confirmation of asset submission (yes/no)
Recovery amount in case asset not submitted

| IT SPOC

|
BYOD reimbursement recovery amount.
Joining bonus
Gratuity amount, if applicable
Notice shortfall amount basis BHR input
In case employee has car lease then he needs to foreclose the loan with leasing company. HR-Ops to take the confirmation from leasing company. (Applicable only for non-GEC members)

| HR Ops Exit SPOC

|

Timeline: The timeline to complete the above process is Last Working Day plus additional 14 days.

Consolidation and Upload of Clearance Input:

Policy on prevention of sexual harassement (POSH) at workplace

Policy Title
| Prevention of Sexual Harassment at workplace
|
Applicability
| Applicable to all full-time employees of Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.
|
Coverage
| Policy on Prevention of Sexual Harassment framework
Internal Committee
Complaint Mechanism
|
Prepared by
| Team, Compensation & Benefits
|
Reviewed By
| Head - Compensation & Benefits
|
Approved By
| Chief Human Resources Officer
|

Effective date

|
|

The prevention of sexual harassment at the workplace policy is a set of guidelines and procedures implemented by organizations to create a safe and respectful working environment for all employees.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in the Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that this policy version shall supersede all earlier versions. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required. Notwithstanding, Meridian Finance will follow the prevailing statutory requirements at the point of any application / notification.

Contents

1.Preamble 4
1.1Policy Objective 4
1.2 Policy Management 4
1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation 4
1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates 5
1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance 5

Preamble

Our Company has a philosophy that includes respect for human values, individual dignity, no gender bias and adherence to honest, ethical and professional conduct among Employees. Employees are guided by the vision statement and values of the organization as modified from time to time for the success and reputation of the Company.
Protection against Sexual Harassment and right to work with dignity are universally recognized human rights. Company is committed to creating a healthy working environment and promotes equality of opportunity and freedom that enables Employees to work without fear of prejudice, gender bias and Sexual Harassment.

The Company also believes that all its Employees have the right to be treated with dignity. Sexual Harassment at Workplace is a violation of the fundamental right and, therefore, requires an eﬀective mechanism for prevention, prohibition, and redressal of Sexual Harassment, and as such necessitates a policy in conformity with the applicable laws and rules.

This Policy is in line with The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.

Policy Objective
The objectives of this Policy are threefold:

To define Sexual Harassment;
To lay down the guidelines for making Complaints; and
To provide the procedure for conciliation, resolution and redressal of Complaints in a time bound manner.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________. The terms and conditions contained herein must be adhered to when making an agreement between the Company and the business traveller in relation to travel for business purpose, as long as they are compatible with national legislation.

The Company’s POSH committee will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates
The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The policy is in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations related to sexual harassment.
The procedures for reporting incidents of sexual harassment are outlined in the policy. Employees have the right to report incidents without fear of retaliation.
All reports of sexual harassment will be treated with confidentially to the extent possible, while still conducting a thorough investigation.
The company is committed in providing regular training and awareness programs on sexual harassment prevention. All employees, including managers and supervisors, will receive training to understand their rights and responsibilities and to promote a respectful work environment.

Applicability
The Policy is applicable to all the employees of Meridian Finance and all its current subsidiaries and such other subsidiaries that may become subsidiaries from time to time, irrespective of their level, rank or designations across all departments, functions, operations, units, meeting centres and offices (including, branch, administrative and regional) of the Company and is deemed to be incorporated in the service conditions of all the Company employees and comes into eﬀect forthwith.

Where Sexual Harassment occurs at Workplace as a result of an act or omission by any Third Party or outsider, the Company will take all steps necessary and reasonable to assist the Aggrieved Person in terms of support and preventive action.

Definitions

For the purpose of the Policy, unless the context otherwise requires:
“Aggrieved Person” means in relation to a Workplace, a person, of any age whether employed or not, who alleges to have been subjected to any act of Sexual harassment by the Respondent.
“Complaint” means a complaint of Sexual Harassment at Workplace.

“Committee” means an Internal Committee constituted for redressal of Complaints by the Aggrieved Person and make recommendations for resolution to the Management Team.

“Employee” means a person employed at a Workplace for any work on regular, temporary, ad hoc or daily wages basis, either directly or through an agent, including a contractor, with or, without the knowledge of the principal employer, whether for remuneration or not, or working on a voluntary basis or otherwise, whether the terms of employment are express or implied, and includes a co-worker, a contract worker, probationer, trainee, apprentice or called by any other such name;
Explanation: The aforesaid definition of ‘Employee’ shall be used only for the purposes of the Policy and cannot be used to claim rights of an employee conferred by any law for the time being in force.

“Management Team” shall mean the person/s vested with the powers to take appropriate action for implementing the decision of the Committee and shall consist of such officers as designated by the Company from time to time;

“Respondent” means a person against whom the Aggrieved Person has made a Complaint.

“Sexual Harassment” includes any one or more of the following unwelcome acts or behavior (whether directly or by implication) namely:
Physical contact and advances; or
a demand or request for sexual favours; or
making sexually coloured remarks; or
showing pornography; or
any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature.

The following circumstances, among other circumstances, if it occurs or is present in relation to or connected with any act or behavior of Sexual Harassment may amount to Sexual Harassment:
implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in employment; or
implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in employment: or
implied or explicit threat about present or future employment status; or
interference with work or creating an intimidating or oﬀensive or hostile work environment; or
humiliating treatment likely to aﬀect health or safety.

“Third Party” means any person or persons not on the rolls of the Company but, in the course of work-related activities, interacting with the Company.

“Workplace” shall mean any place(s) where an Aggrieved Person is employed or works, or visits in connection with their duties during the course of or arising out of their employment and includes transportation provided by the employer for undertaking such journey.

Prevention of Sexual Harassment at Workplace & Reporting

No Employee shall be subjected to Sexual Harassment at any Workplace. If an Employee is being sexually harassed, the employee should:

Expressly communicate to the Respondent that their behavior is unwelcome and ask them to stop;
Keep a record of incidents (dates, times, locations, possible witness, what happened, his/her response). It is not mandatory to have a record of events to file a Complaint, but a record can strengthen the Aggrieved Person’s case and help the Aggrieved Person remembers the details over time, in case the Complaint is not filed immediately;
Make, in writing, a Complaint to the Committee within a period of 1 (one) year from the date of last incident in accordance with the terms of the Policy

Internal Committee

The Committee shall consist of not less than four members, to be nominated by the Company. Provided that at least one-half of the total members so nominated shall be women.

The Committee shall be headed by a woman employed at a senior level at Workplace, who shall be its presiding officer;

Not less than two members of the Committee shall be from amongst Employees preferably committed to the cause of women or who have had experience in social work or have legal knowledge;

One member of the Committee shall be from amongst non-governmental organization or associations committed to the cause of women or a person familiar with the issues relating to Sexual Harassment;

The presiding officer and members of the Committee shall hold office for such period, not exceeding three years, from the date of their nomination;

The names, email ids and contact details of the presiding officer and other members of the Committee(s), to be constituted at all the offices of the Company shall be communicated through a separate circular.

Complaint Mechanism

Complaint to be made in writing:
A Complaint may be made in writing to the Committee as per the format prescribed under Annexure - 1 at wecare@meridianfinance.com or at the email id of any member of the Committee. Alternatively, the complaint can also be sent as per the said format at the following address:
Ms. the HR SPOC, Presiding Officer - Complaints Committee, Meridian Finance, Brindavan, Vidyanagari Marg, CST Road, Kalina, Santacruz (East), Mumbai, 400 098

In case the Aggrieved Person is unable to make the Complaint in writing, they may approach the presiding officer or any member of the Committee, who shall render all assistance to the Aggrieved Person for making the Complaint in writing.

The Complaint shall be addressed to the Sexual Harassment Committee and shall contain all the material and relevant details concerning the alleged Sexual Harassment at Workplace including, the name of the Respondent(s) and the name of the Aggrieved Person along with the names and addresses of the witnesses and supporting documents.

At the time of filing the Complaint, the complainant shall submit six copies of the Complaint along with the names and addresses of the witnesses and supporting documents.

The following persons can make a complaint:
Aggrieved Person
In case of physical incapacity of the Aggrieved Person the Complaint can be filed by:
A relative or a friend or a co-worker of the Aggrieved Person; or
An officer of the National Commission of Women or State Women’s Commission: (this is applicable only when the Aggrieved Person is a woman): or
Any person who has knowledge of the incident, with the written consent of the Aggrieved Person.

In case of mental incapacity of the Aggrieved Person the Complaint can be filed by:
A relative or a friend of the Aggrieved Person; or
A special educator; or
A qualified psychiatrist or psychologist; or
The guardian or authority under whose care the Aggrieved Person is receiving treatment or care; or
Any person who has knowledge of the incident jointly with a relative or a friend of the Aggrieved Person or a special educator or a qualified psychiatrist or psychologist, or the guardian or authority under whose care the Aggrieved Person is receiving treatment or care.

In case of death of the Aggrieved Person the Complaint can be filed by any person who has knowledge of the incident with the written consent of the legal heir of the Aggrieved Person.

In case the Aggrieved Person is unable to make a Complaint for any reason the
Complaint can be filed by any person who has knowledge of the incident with the written consent of the Aggrieved Person.

Timeline for making the Complaint:

A Complaint should be made within a period of 1 (one) year from the date of the incident and in case of series of incidents, within a period of 1 (one) year from the date of the last incident.

Inquiry to Complaint:
Manner of Inquiry:

The Internal Committee shall proceed to make inquiry into the Complaint where the Respondent is an Employee.
On the receipt of the Complaint, the Committee shall, within 7 (seven) working days from the date of receipt of the Complaint, send a copy of the Complaint received from the Aggrieved Person to the Respondent.
The Respondent shall file his/her reply to the Committee along with the names and addresses of the witnesses and supporting documents within a period not exceeding 07 (seven) working days.
The Committee shall make an enquiry into the Complaint in accordance with the principles of natural justice.
The Aggrieved Person and the Respondent shall not be allowed to bring in any legal practitioner to represent them in their case at any stage of the proceedings before the Committee.
In conducting the inquiry, a minimum of 3 (three) members of the Committee including the presiding officer shall be present.
The parties shall, during the course of inquiry, be given an opportunity of being heard and a copy of the findings shall be made available to both the Aggrieved Person and the Respondent to enable them to make representation against the findings before the Committee.
For the purpose of making an inquiry, the Committee shall have the same powers as are vested in a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908) when trying a suit in respect of the following matters, namely: --
summoning and enforcing the attendance of any person and examining him on oath;
requiring the discovery and production of documents: and
any other matter which may be prescribed.

The inquiry shall be completed within a period of ninety days.

Actions during pendency of Enquiry:

During the pendency of an inquiry the Committee at the written request of the Aggrieved Person may recommend to the Management Team to:
transfer the Aggrieved Person or the Respondent to any other Workplace; or
grant leave to the Aggrieved Person up to a period of 3 (three) months; or
restrain the Respondent from reporting on the work or writing his/her confidential report and assign the same to another person.

The leave granted to the Aggrieved Person under this recommendation shall be in addition to the leave that she would be otherwise entitled.

The Committee if so, required may issue appropriate interim orders from time to time recommending the Management Team to issue orders as may be necessary to ensure the safety of the Aggrieved Person and/or the witnesses.

On recommendations of the Committee, the Management Team shall implement the recommendations of the Committee and send the report of such implementation to the Committee.

Termination of Inquiry Proceedings / Ex parte Decision

The Committee shall have the right to terminate the inquiry proceedings or give an ex parte decision on the Complaint, if the complainant or Respondent fails, without sufficient cause, to present herself or himself for 3 (three) consecutive hearings conveyed by the presiding officer of the Committee.

Provided such termination or ex parte order shall not be passed unless a 15 (fifteen) days prior written notice has been given to the party concerned.

Inquiry Report

On the completion of the inquiry, the Committee shall provide a report of its findings to the Management Team within a period of 10 (ten) days from the date of completion of the inquiry and such report shall be made available to the complainant and Respondent.

The Committee may recommend a detailed and reasoned order, which may include:

Recommending to the Management Team to take appropriate action for Sexual Harassment as a misconduct in accordance with the HR Manual / terms of employment and/or payment of compensation, commensurate with the gravity of the oﬀence of which the Respondent has been found guilty of as per applicable law;

to deduct, from the salary or wages of the Respondent such sum as it may consider appropriate to be paid to the Aggrieved Person or to their legal heirs, provided that in case Company is unable to make such deduction from the salary of the Respondent due to they being absent from duty or cessation of employment, it may direct to the Respondent to pay such sum to the Aggrieved Person

Recommending to the Management Team the steps necessary and reasonable to assist the Aggrieved Person in terms of support and preventive action where Sexual Harassment at Workplace has occurred as a result of an act or omission by any Third Party or outsider;

Recommending to the Management Team the appropriate disciplinary action against the person making the Complaint, in case the Complaint registered is found to be frivolous or false or was made with a malicious intention;

Recommending to the Management Team that no action is required to be taken in the matter, in case it arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the Respondent has not been proved.

The Company shall act upon the recommendation within sixty days of its receipt from the Committee.

Confidentiality
Information generated in the course of informal reviews and formal investigations necessary for enforcing this Policy will be given the full extent of confidentiality to Employee personnel records. Any person who, without authorization, reveals such information will be subject to disciplinary action.

The sharing of the content of the Complaints will be on a “need to know” basis only. It is understood that Sexual Harassment at Workplace is an issue of highly sensitive nature and therefore strict confidentiality will be maintained by the Aggrieved Person, witnesses, the Complainant, Committee and the Management Team.
Protection Against Retaliation

Regardless of the outcome of the Complaint made in good faith, the Aggrieved Person lodging the Complaint and any person providing information or any witness, will be protected from any form of retaliation. While dealing with Complaints, the Committee shall ensure that the Aggrieved Person or the witness are not victimized or discriminated against by the Respondent. Any unwarranted pressures, retaliatory or any other type of unethical behavior from the Respondent against the Aggrieved Person while the investigation is in progress should be reported by the Aggrieved Person to the Committee as soon as possible. Disciplinary action will be recommended by the Committee to the Management Team against any such Complaints.
Complaint made with a Malicious Intent

The Policy has been evolved as a tool to ensure that Employees have a forum to approach the Company in the event of instances of Sexual Harassment at Workplace. Where the Committee arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the Respondent is malicious or the Aggrieved Person or the person making the Complaint has made the Complaint knowing it to be false or the Aggrieved Person or any other person making the Complaint has produced any forged or misleading documents, it may recommend appropriate disciplinary against the complainant. The persons who are victims of such frivolous or false complaints may, in addition to the above, seek legal remedies as may be provided under the various laws for the time being in force.

This Performance Management Policy outlines the provisions for employee-related performance. This policy guidelines will explain how the performance of an employee will be assessed.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy manual should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to WorkApps Product Solutions Private Limited & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that all policies and processes stipulated in this version shall supersede those set out in any earlier versions of the HR manual. WorkApps Product Solutions Private Limited will endeavour to update this policy as required.

INTRODUCTION

In WorkApps Product Solutions Private Limited, Performance management culture is designed in such a way that all the employees understand the Company’s mission & Goals and align their performance to achieve those goals. The individuals and teams are appropriately empowered and are rewarded according to their contributions to the Organization Goals.

1.1 Policy Objective

The overall objectives of the policy are to:

Ensure that every employee understands how their role contributes to the company’s success by aligning individual goals with business objectives.
Provide employees with clear performance expectations and a pathway to success
Establish a fair and transparent process that holds employees accountable for their performance and ensures equal treatment
Regularly review and enhance the Performance Management System to incorporate best practices and adapt to changing needs
To appreciate, recognize and to give reward and compensate employees for achievement of performance objectives successfully in a more objective, transparent and justified way.

1.2 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Compensation & Benefits Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require the CHRO’s written approval.

1.3 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.4 Roles and Responsibilities

Responsibilities of the Employee:
The employees are responsible for actively participating in the goal-setting process. This involves collaborating with their managers to establish clear and measurable performance objectives that align with the organization's overall goals.
Employees are required to actively participate in performance reviews and provide honest and constructive feedback about their own performance. This includes reflecting on their achievements, identifying areas for improvement, and discussing their career aspirations and development needs.

Responsibilities of the Immediate Supervisor
Collaborating with employees to set clear and achievable performance goals that align with the organization's objectives.
Conducting formal performance evaluations to assess employee performance, identify strengths and areas for improvement, and provide constructive feedback.
Providing guidance, support, and coaching to help employees improve their performance and develop their skills and competencies

Responsibilities of the BHRs
To ensure that the employees have updated their goal sheet within the given timeline
To ensure that the employees are having their regular performance check-ins with their immediate supervisor to discuss their goal achievements.
To ensure that employees are timely updating the self-evaluation sheet in the system
To ensure that there is formal appraisal discussion taking place between the manager and the employee before publishing the ratings to the employee

Responsibilities of Skip Level Manager
To ensure that the goal of the company and the unit/department is cascaded down to all the employees, such that the organization goals are inline with the individual KRAs.
To participate in the calibration sessions and reviewing performance evaluations, they help maintain consistency in performance ratings across teams.

Responsibilities of C&B Team
Responsible for preparing the bell curve, PLI (Performance Linked Incentive), and increment budget.
They are tasked with creating a base file for each platform, ensuring accurate and comprehensive data for performance evaluations.
Responsible for uploading PLI and increment data onto the the HR portal platform, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.
responsible for ensuring that appraisal letters are correctly issued to employees through the the HR portal platform, reflecting performance evaluations accurately.

Responsibility of the HR Operations team
They are responsible employer is responsible for sharing monthly closure files & basic details of the employees with C&B team.

Responsibility of the Finance Team
This team is responsible for sharing achievement data of the organization with C&B team

Responsibility of CHRO/MD
They are responsible for approving the following:
Bell curve
PLI and
Increment budget

Responsibility of the Payroll Processing Team
This team is responsible for releasing the annual PLI amounts to the employees

Scope

This policy is applicable to all the eligible employees on the rolls of WorkApps Product Solutions Private Limited & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Performance Management

Eligibility:

All employee excluding contractual employees joined on or before 31st Dec of the current FY.
Employees who have joined post 31st Dec of the current FY, the proportionate PLI would be considered in next increment cycle and will be excluded from the current appraisal cycle.

Performance Management Process:

The appraisal process, also called a performance review or evaluation, is a systematic way to assess an employee's work over a period of time. Performance Culture is designed in such a way that all employees understand the Company’s mission and goals and align their performance to achieve those goals. The individuals and teams are appropriately empowered and are rewarded according to their contribution to the Organization’s goals.

Performance Management Process involves the following key steps:

Goal Setting - Goal setting is to enable individuals to define their desired outcomes and create a roadmap for achieving them. It involves identifying specific targets, outlining the steps needed to reach them, and establishing a timeline for completion. These goals should be aligned with the company’s mission. This process takes place from 12th May to 31st May, where Key Result Areas (KRAs) are set for all employees after discussion with IS and DH.

Mid-Term Review, At WorkApps Product Solutions Private Limited, feedback is an on-going process where supervisor shares feedback for their team member’s performance. During a mid-term review, managers assess employee progress on their key result areas (KRAs) and provide feedback to guide their development. This process takes place from 9th Oct to 26th Oct.

Annual Appraisal, It is an annual process which happens at the end of the financial year. It involves assessment of the employee against the KRAs set in the start of the year. The process takes place on the HR portal from 6th March to 26th march and annual appraisal consolidation happens from 15th April to 30th April. The overall rating is finalized in discussion with HR and executive committee for Annual Increment.

Budget Approval - Upper management reviews and approves final increment and PLI budget for all business units according to their performance. Budgeting takes place in 1st week of April.

Letter Generation and Release - Final letters are released to the employees from 27th April to 30th April.

Timeline:

The performance review period is scheduled between 1st April and 31st March.
The effective date of salary increment is 1st June of every year.

Goal Setting

Introduction

As part of the performance review process, it is essential to emphasize the significance of goal setting in the financial year. The job responsibilities of an employee need to be accomplished by well-defined goals that are aligned with the company's mission and overarching strategic objectives.
For this reason, a comprehensive goal setting exercise is carried out for the entire organization. Each of the Senior Management team members decides on a process or methodology to cascade the goals to the members of their team, till the last person. The Senior Management functionary concerned may also take a review of the previous year’s performance: what went well and what are the opportunities for improvement.
The Goals set by the employees should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound

Goal Setting Process:

The manager and employee receive mails for setting the annual goals. There should be at least one discussion between the manager and the employee to discuss the goal and priorities of the year.
It is recommended that the employee has 3-5 KRAs aligned with the organization Goals after having it discussed with the Manager.
While updating the KRAs and Goals in the HR portal, there are major three fields to be needed:
Goals: These encompass broad objectives such as "Improve employee retention by reducing turnover.
KPIs: Measurable metrics are identified to track progress, such as Employee Turnover Rate, Employee Engagement Score, Time to Fill Open Positions.
Targets: Specific and measurable milestones are set within a defined timeframe, for example, reducing employee turnover rate by 5% in the next year
Specific and measurable milestones are set within a defined timeframe, for example, reducing employee turnover rate by 5% in the next year
Once employees have entered their goals on the the HR portal platform, they are automatically sent to their respective managers for approval.

Timelines:

This process is to be conducted between 12th May and 31st May of each year.

Mid Term Review

Introduction
During a mid-term review, managers undertake a comprehensive assessment of employee progress on their key result areas (KRAs). This evaluation involves analysing the extent to which employees have achieved their defined goals and objectives. Managers provide valuable feedback based on this assessment, offering guidance and insights to help employees refine their development plans and enhance their performance. The mid-term review serves as a crucial checkpoint to ensure that employees are on track and aligned with organizational goals, fostering continuous improvement and professional growth.

Mid Term Review Process

As part of the mid-term review process, managers and employees receive emails notifying them about the upcoming review. These emails serve as a reminder and provide instructions on how to proceed with the review.
During the mid-term review, managers and employees engage in one-on-one discussions to assess progress and performance in each Key Result Area (KRA). These discussions provide an opportunity for the manager and employee to have a focused conversation about the employee's goals, achievements, challenges, and any necessary adjustments or support needed.
During the mid-term review, managers and employees engage in one-on-one discussions to assess progress and performance in each Key Result Area (KRA). These discussions provide an opportunity for the manager and employee to have a focused conversation about the employee's goals, achievements, challenges, and any necessary adjustments or support needed.
Managers on the the HR portal platform provide evaluations for each Key Result Area. These evaluations are categorized into different levels, such as "Does not meet expectations," "Meets most expectations," "Meets expectations," "Often exceeds expectations," and "Far exceeds expectations." This allows for a comprehensive assessment of an employee's performance.
After receiving feedback from their managers, employees take note of the feedback provided and acknowledge it on the the HR portal platform.
The mid-term review process is finalized and then completed on the the HR portal platform.

Timelines:

This process is to be conducted between 9th October and 26th October of each year.

Annual Appraisal
Introduction

Assessing the annual performance of the employee based on the established KRAs to determine the final rating. Both employee and manager have to give their evaluation.

Annual Appraisal Process

Email sent to managers and employees for conducting annual appraisal.
Employees do self-evaluation by providing themselves the given reviews on each KRA:
Does not meet expectations,
Meets most expectations,
Meets expectations,
Often exceeds expectations,
Far exceeds expectations.
One on one discussion with manager on each KRA.
Managers on the HR portal provide reviews on each KRA:
Does not meet expectations,
Meets most expectations,
Meets expectations,
Often exceeds expectations,
Far exceeds expectations.
The final rating is given to the employees according to the Bell Curve fitment.
BHRs of each business have discussion with the top management and then final rating is given to each employee.
These final ratings are then uploaded by C&B team on the HR portal.
Closure on the HR portal for annual appraisal.

Timelines:

Annual Appraisal on the HR portal, 6th March to 26th March
Annual Appraisal Consolidation, 15th April to 30th April
Budgeting

Introduction

Upper management reviews and approves final increment and PLI budget for all business units according to their performance.

Annual Appraisal Process

Obtaining detail from Finance: Data of actual vs achievement to be obtained from the finance team for budget preparation.
Preparation of bell-curve, PLI and increment budget: C&B team to prepare platform wise bell-curve, PLI and increment budget based on the data received from the finance team.
Approval from CHRO & MD on platform wise bell-curve & increment budget:
C&B team shares the PLI and increment budget proposal with CHRO for his approval.
If there are any remarks on the budget, same shall be addressed by the C&B team.
If the budget is approved by the CHRO, same shall be shared to the MD for his approval by the CHRO.
Creation of platform wise files and sharing it with the business HR team for seeking its inputs:
Eligible employees shall be identified for each platform as per the eligibility criteria.
Eligible PLI payable for each employee shall be calculated. Month on month PLI shall be plotted against each employee. Summation of PLI payable for each employee for all the month shall be target PLI payable.
Platform wise base file shall be shared with business HR team for seeking its inputs.
Verifying and sharing the base files with CHRO and MD:
Base file received from business HR team shall be collated by C&B team.
C&B team shall send the collated file to CHRO for approval.
If there are any remarks highlighted by CHRO, same shall be addressed by the C&B team.
Post verification by CHRO, base file shall be sent to MD for his approval.
Communication of the final rating and amount is sent to all the heads of the department.
Upload of PLI & increment data on the HR portal: C&B team to upload data on the HR portal for letter generation.
Generation of appraisal letters for all the employees: Post upload of PLI and increment on the HR portal, appraisal letters will be issued to all the employees.
Payment of annual PLI: Post release of the appraisal letters to all the employees, annual PLI amount shall be paid to the employees.
(PLI, Credit before 30th April
Increment, June Salary Cycle)

Timelines:

Budgeting takes place in the 1st week of April.

Letter Generation and Release Process

Letter Design and Configuration

Each form of appraisal requires different letter design and configuration. There are various coding schemes for different types of assessments. Each employee has different types of appraisals, thus depending on that, the employees are matched with their required format of appraisal and finally the letter code is assigned to them.
There are designated roles assigned to each employee for the process. For letter generation we have role of - Appraisal Letter Generator. After selecting the option of Appraisal Letter Generator, below window will appear.

There are 3 tabs needed as a part of the letter generation and release process. Please refer Annexure-1 for the detail.

Current Promotion Process -

Introduction

The promotion process outlines the guidelines and procedures that govern how employees are considered and selected for advancement within the company. This policy sets the foundation for a merit-based system that motivates employees, fosters career development, and aligns with the organization's strategic objectives.

This policy document serves as a guide, outlining the company policies and procedures on Health check-up benefits, Mediclaim policies, Accidental and Group Term life insurance policies.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that this policy version shall supersede all earlier versions. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.
