INTRODUCTION

At Meridian Finance, the company understands the importance of taking care of employees' health and well-being. That's why Meridian Finance extends benefits by covering employees and their families with Mediclaim policies and insurance coverage for accidents and life insurance. Also, the Company extends the telemedicine facility for the employees which involves easy and convenient access to virtual health care services and consultation.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objective of the Mediclaim policy is to provide comprehensive health insurance coverage to employees and their families, ensuring access to quality healthcare services and financial protection against medical expenses.
The objective of the Life & Accidental Insurance policy is to provide employees and their families with financial security in the event of accidental injuries, disability, or death. It aims to offer peace of mind by providing a lump sum payment or coverage for medical expenses, ensuring the well-being and financial stability of employees and their family.
The objective of the Telemedicine facility is to provide with the easy healthcare access to the employees regardless of their location or work schedules and facilitating early diagnosis and timely management of health issues through convenient consultations.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s HR Operations will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Annual Health Checkup
Scope

All full-time employees of Meridian Finance are eligible for free annual health check-up, on completion of one year of service.

General Guidelines
Employees of age below 35 may avail this facility once in two years, otherwise it may be availed once every year.
For OL III and above grade, this benefit is extended to the spouse of the employee.
Employees will be eligible for health check-up after completion of 24 months from the date of last health check-up for age below 35 years and 12 months for age 35 and above.
Annual health check-up is a facility provided to employees. Hence, it is not mandatory to undergo a check- up and employees have the discretion to avail this facility.
The list of tests covered in this policy is as decided by the Company. Any additional test cost is to be borne by the employee. Please refer Annexure, 4 for the list of tests covered.

Entitlements
For Mumbai location, employees have the option to avail the facility of Health Check -up from the company’s list of tie-up hospitals or they may also avail the facility from the hospital of their choice and get the amount reimbursed. Please refer Annexure, 5 for the list of company tie-up hospitals in Maharashtra.
For locations other than Mumbai, employees can get the medical check-up done from their choice of hospital and get the amount reimbursed from the company.
The limit for reimbursement in Mumbai is Rs 4,000 and in Non-Mumbai locations is Rs 3500. It is important to submit the original documents for the purpose of reimbursement.
Exceptions
The employees on notice period are not eligible for this benefit.
Any deviation in the policy has to be approved by the CHRO.

Telemedicine, Connect & Heal
Connect & Heal is an integrated platform for all healthcare needs and its end-to-end services manage all care interventions.
This benefit is extended to all the employees of Meridian Finance across all the grades.
Unlimited free virtual consultation with general physician and specialist is provided under this.
Discounted prescribed lab tests and health packages are included in this facility.
Discounted OPD and emergency ambulance service is also provided.
This facility includes discounts on medicine delivery.
Please refer Annexure, 6 for the user manual of the telemedicine support.
Group Mediclaim
Scope
All employees of Meridian Finance are covered under the Group Mediclaim Policy, which provides reimbursement for medical cost incurred during hospitalization.
Eligibility and Entitlements

The benefit is extended to the family members of the employee. This depends on the eligibility as per the grade. Please refer Annexure, 1 for the eligibility matrix and the reimbursement limits.
Under this policy family members are defined as Parents (Father, Mother), Children (2 children - unmarried and below 21 years of age)
This policy is applicable only till the last working day of the employee.
Policy Guidelines

Employees are offered cashless as well as reimbursement facilities through a Third-Party Administrator (TPA) as decided by The Company.
The employees are required to submit details of their dependents in the HR portal portal for availing Mediclaim benefits before the day of hospitalization.
The Coverage amount limit depends on the eligibility as per the employee grade. Expenses beyond the coverage limit shall be borne by the employee.
Maternity Claims have a separate coverage limit as per the grade of the employee and is payable for the delivery of the first two children only.
The coverage is for expenses incurred for any disease or illness for which treatment is taken in a hospital and the hospitalization period is more than 24 Hrs. (except Surgeries for Diseases of Eyes like Cataract, Glaucoma, etc., Hospitalization for Dialysis, Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy & D & C).
Expenses incurred for 30 days pre and 60 days (30 days for Maternity claims) post from the date of hospitalization are also paid. The nature of the diseases covered under this policy is pre-decided by The Company.
Out-patient treatments are not covered under the policy, except treatment of Animal bites, and treatment diagnostics arising out of Accident.
Employees may/are required to get the medical card (Mandatory) generated from the TPA. This card may be used to get cashless treatment of the employee of his/her family member.
Any deviation in the policy has to be approved by the CHRO.

Group Life Insurance

Scope and Purpose
All permanent employees of Meridian Finance are covered under Group Term Life Insurance, to provide insurance cover to family members of the employee in an event of death of him/her due to any reason (natural / unnatural / accidental, except suicide committed within first year from date of joining the company).

Eligibility and Entitlements

The policy is applicable only to the employees and is not extended to his/her family members.
The insurance coverage is based on the company’s employment grade of an employee. Please refer Annexure, 2 for the grade wise coverage amount eligibility.

Policy Guidelines

The employees are to submit the details of the nominee/s at the time of joining or as and when there is any change in the nominee/s, in written application to the HR department.
The group term life insurance benefit ceases after the employee exits from the company (voluntarily / involuntarily).
Any deviation in the policy has to be approved by the CHRO.
Group Personal Accident Insurance

Scope and Purpose
All permanent employees of Meridian Finance are covered under Group Personal Accident Insurance, to provide insurance cover to family members of the employee in an event of death of him/her due to an accident or to cover potential risk of loss in earning capacity of an employee arising out of an accident or even death.

Eligibility and Entitlements
The policy is applicable only to the employee and is not extended to his/her family members.
The insurance coverage is based on the company’s employment grade of an employee or the nature of injury causing the disability / loss in earning capacity. Please refer Annexure, 3 for the grade wise coverage amount eligibility.

Policy Guidelines
The policy does not cover the reimbursement of expenses incurred towards medical treatment in such accidents.
In case of accident causing the disability / loss in earning capacity, intimation to HR department shall be provided within 10 days from date of an accident.
The group personal accident insurance benefit ceases after the employee exits from the company (voluntarily / involuntarily).
Any deviation in the policy has to be approved by the CHRO.

POLICIES on internal job posting

Policy Title
| Policy on Internal Job Posting
|
Applicability
| Applicable to all full-time employees of Workapps Product Solutions Private Limited & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.
|
Coverage
| Guidelines on Ascend
Guidelines on Aspire
|
Prepared by
| Team, Compensation & Benefits
|
Reviewed By
| Head - Compensation & Benefits
|
Approved By
| Chief Human Resources Officer
|
Effective date
|
|

This policy documents guidelines and procedures established by organizations to facilitate the process of filling job vacancies with existing employees. These policies aim to promote internal mobility, career development, and employee engagement within the company.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy manual should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Workapps Product Solutions Private Limited & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that all policies and processes stipulated in this version shall supersede those set out in any earlier versions. Workapps Product Solutions Private Limited will endeavour to update this policy as required. Notwithstanding, Workapps Product Solutions Private Limited will follow the prevailing statutory requirements at the point of any application / notification.

Contents

1.INTRODUCTION 4
1.1 Policy objectives: 4
1.2 Policy Management 4

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates 4
2.Ascend 4

3.Aspire 7

INTRODUCTION

Workapps Product Solutions Private Limited encourages employees and provide opportunity for talent mobility within the Group companies. This enables employees to gain varied exposure and experience in different roles and business set ups. The company has two programmes on Internal Job Posting (IJP) namely Ascend and Aspire. This document summarises the guidelines and procedure on these two programmes.

1.1 Policy objectives:
The overall objectives of the policy are:

This policy aims to provide employees with opportunities for growth and advancement within the organization.
This policy help organizations to retain the top performers by offering them opportunities to explore new roles and challenges within the company.
This policy promote a culture of continuous learning and development within the organization. By encouraging employees to apply for new positions and take on different responsibilities, organizations can foster a dynamic and innovative work environment.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________. The Company’s Compensation & Benefits Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates
The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Ascend
Definition:
“Ascend” an Internal Job posting program that provides an opportunity for employees to gain varied exposure in various businesses/ roles and helps in leveraging our human capital.
It provides opportunities to employees for learning, self-development and career growth by working in their area of interest, thereby, develop new skill sets during their tenure with Meridian Finance.

Eligibility:
Tenure: Employees must have a minimum tenure of two years in their current role.
Rating: Employees must have received a minimum rating of 3 in their last two performance appraisal cycles.
Grade: All employees within the grade range of FL III to OL I are eligible to apply.
Grade Limit: Employees can apply for internal job postings up to two grades above their current grade, provided they meet the criteria for the advertised position.
Disciplinary Check: There should not be any ongoing RCU / HR investigations against the employee.

IJP Publishing and Selection:
Posting of Positions: All positions, except for sensitive positions, will be posted for internal job posting. The Head of Business Human Resources (BHR) will have the authority to determine and approve which positions are considered sensitive.
Application Period: Positions will be open for a period of 7 days for employees to apply through the internal job posting process.
Notification to Current Supervisor: Applicants are not required to inform their current supervisor before submitting their application for an internal job posting.
Selection Process:
Selection process will be completed in 7 days from closure of IJP applications.
One Panel interview will be done for applicants who meet the IJP requirement.
Business panel to be at least two grades above the role requirement.
HR representative is mandatory in the panel.
Once selected by panel, no further approvals are required for offering the new role. HR to communicate to the HoD of selected employee of his/ her selection in IJP.
No approval is required from the current department.
Post selection, employee must be released to the new department / role within 60 days. It is mandatory to release the selected employee post 60 days. HR must maintain the confidentiality of the movement during the selection process.
Grade and Salary Fitment:
For same grade movement:
If the current grade of the employee is same as the grade of the new role, there will be no change in the grade or salary.
For higher grade movement:
If the current grade is lower than the grade of the new role, grade re-fitment and salary re-fitment will be done by HR (max. up to 1 grade)
Salary re-fitment will be done as per the internal parity of the new role, max. up to P25 of the role.
Guard Rails:
Re-application: Employee can re-apply for as many roles unless already selected for an IJP.
Post selection, employee is not eligible for applying for another IJP for 2 years.
During the interaction with the panel, if the candidate feels the job is not suitable, candidate may back-out at the stage of IJP panel interview itself. Backing out at a later stage will not be acceptable.
If employee fails to take up new responsibilities, he/she will be barred from the IJP process.
PMS Ratings after Selection:
PMS Rating will be monitored for all IJP transfers centrally.
Explanation will be sought in case of rating drop compared to previous year (not more than 1 rating drop)
Any deviations to the above will be investigated by HR team and approval from respective GEC will be sought.
If an employee joins the new role on or after 1st October, rating decision will be taken by the new department with inputs from previous supervisor.
If an employee joins the new role on or before 30th September, rating decision will be taken by the new department.
Minimum 3 rating is to be retained in the appraisal post IJP.

Responsibilities:

For HR:
Respective Business HR will post Internal Job Postings on a monthly basis through the HR portal for all positions except sensitive positions.
For sensitive positions, approval to be taken from Head BHR
Navigation for BHR for posting IJP: the HR portal > Change profile to Business HR (TA) > Talent Acquisition > Sourcing > Publish Requirement > Select requisition number > Publish Info > Click on View > Apply.
For employees:
IJP mail / posters will be sent to employees informing them about the positions open for Internal Job Postings from the ID: ijp@meridianfinance.com
Navigation for employees to view and apply for IJP:
Visit the HR portal> Home> Talent Acquisition> About Me> Internal Job Posting
Search for the requisition no. for the position you are applying for Click on View > Apply.
The said position will be available on the IJP Portal for a period of 7 days.

Aspire
Definition:

” Aspire” is the Internal Job posting program at Workapps Product Solutions Private Limited. It provides an opportunity for employees to gain varied exposure in Group companies / businesses and helps in leveraging our human capital.
Aspire helps an employee to develop new skill sets and hence provide opportunities for self- development and career growth by working in their area of interest.

Eligibility:
Following criteria needs to be fulfilled before applying for Aspire.
Tenure: The employee must have completed a minimum tenure of 12 months in their current role or current Business Unit, either in one role or multiple roles.
Rating: The employee's overall rating should be "3" (meets expectations) or above in the last two years' performance evaluations.
Grade Limit: The position for which the employee is applying should not be more than two job grades higher than their current job grade, provided they meet all the criteria for the advertised position.
Application Limit: An employee is eligible to apply for a maximum of two published positions during the current financial year.

Scope:
The Aspire process is applicable to the following role movements in the Micro Loan Business:
Frontline Employee (FLO) being promoted to Branch Process Manager (BPM)
Branch Process Manager (BPM) being promoted to Branch Manager (BM)
Frontline Collection Officer (FCO) being promoted to Area Collection Manager (ACM)
Branch Manager (BM) being promoted to Territory Manager (TM)
IJP Publishing and Selection:
Internal Job Opportunities are published on ‘ASPIRE ‘, and an email communication is sent to all employees informing them about the open IJP's with its eligibility, job specification etc.
Grade and Salary Fitment:

Grade Change:

Employees are eligible for a grade change only when they are transitioning from an FL IV role to a higher role.

Salary Increment:

Salary increments occur in two cases:

When the employee's take-home salary needs to be protected.
When there is a grade change from FL IV to FL III. The HR Manager has the discretion to make this decision.

ASPIRE Process

Shortlisting Basis Performance:
For shortlisting a pool of employees, we look at vintage, performance rating and recent performance. The threshold performance against each criterion will be decided in the month when the Aspire process for that role is executed.

Process Descriptions:
Vacancies for a particular role are projected for the forthcoming quarter by the help of BHRs.
Product team shares the list of candidates according to the pre-defined criteria. Criteria for different roles are mentioned in Annexure, 1.
The selected candidates are checked by L&D team for RCU eligibility and the candidates with RCU observations in past 1 year are removed from the list.

Associated Risk and Resolutions:
In case of lesser pool size getting selected from a state or region, then the BHRs are advised to go for external recruitment
When there is no Performance criteria defined, Performance rating of 3 is ensured for a quality pool. Business performance is variable on market conditions, but it is ensured that only above average performers get shortlisted.

Assessment:
The assessments conducted are in the form of Online Test or Interviews or a combination of both.

Process Descriptions:
The candidates selected after the RCU check are eligible for the Aspire assessment.
The assessments are according to the role movement:
For movement from Frontline Employee (FLO) to Branch Process Manager (BPM): There are 40 questions on ML products asked in an online test. Followed by interview with the DZM/Senior RMs and BHR.
For movement from Branch Process Manager (BPM) to Branch Manager (BM): There needs to be a recommendation from RPM on people management ability. Followed by Interview with Senior RMs and Zonal Head HR
For movement from Frontline Collection Officer (FCO) to Area Collection Manager (ACM): There are 40 questions on Collections asked in an online test. There needs to be a recommendation from RCM on people management ability. Followed by Interview with Senior Regional Collection Manager and Zonal Head HR
For movement from Branch Manager (BM) to Territory Manager (TM): There needs to be a recommendation from RM on people management ability. Followed by Interview with Senior Regional Collection Manager and Zonal Head HR and then an interview with the Zonal Manager.
For Online test the credentials and dates for the test are sent via SMS to the candidates by the L&D Team Member. The test results are continuously monitored and the BHRs are informed of the status to ensure timely completion
For the interview process the interview evaluation sheet is shared to the Rural HR Team conducting the interviews. Mobility of the candidates is checked in the interview. The interview process is tracked via live Google Sheets where the Rural HR Team updates the status candidate wise. The People management recommendation is also tracked via the same sheet.

Associated Risk and Resolutions:
Integrity of Online Test: The online tests are proctored for Multiple-face detection, Multiple times exam screen minimization and multiple logins.
Integrity on the Interview Process: Interviewers conducting the interviews are required to submit the Interview evaluation sheets to the L&D Team. To ensure quality of the interview all interview panellists are trained and certified in Interviewing Skills.
The interview evaluation forms are in Annexure, 1

Training
The selected participants undergo training. The training focuses on role & responsibilities and behavioural competencies that ensure superior performances in the role.

Process Descriptions:
The employees selected post assessment process have to undergo functional and behavioural training.
Following is the training detail according to the role movement:
For movement from Frontline Employee (FLO) to Branch Process Manager (BPM): It is a 2-day training process.
Day 1: BPM role and responsibilities
Day 2: Grooming, Email etiquette, Planning, Collaboration Detail

For movement from Branch Process Manager (BPM) to Branch Manager (BM): It is a 3-day training process
Day 1: Company and ML business overview
Day 2: BM role and responsibilities
Day 3: Planning. Time Management, Communication Skills, Accountability and Team Management

For movement from Frontline Collection Officer (FCO) to Area Collection Manager (ACM): It is a 3-day training process
Day 1: ACM role and responsibilities, MIS interpretation and Incentive Plan
Day 2: Negotiation Skills, Communication skill, Detail Orientation and Accountability
Day 3: Team Management

For movement from Branch Manager (BM) to Territory Manager (TM): It is a 3-day training process
Day 1: TM role and responsibilities
Day 2: Building and managing reputation, barriers to productivity, planning and accountability
Day 3: Team Management

Associated Risk and Resolutions:
Training Content Delivered: To ensure the quality of the content, the training content is prepared by the product team and approved by the Business Head. The content is updated quarterly.
Training Effectiveness: The effectiveness of the training is ensured by post training assessment and tracking of performance post training is done by the Central HR Team.

Pool for next role
Post training post the Aspire pool is circulated to the ZHRs, BHRs and Central HR Team.

Associated Risk and Resolutions:
Underutilization of the pool: L&D team member weekly tracks the utilization of the Aspire pool created post the training. If any region or state does not have a pool they have to go for external recruitment.
Candidates in the pool for a longer time: L&D team member weekly tracks the utilization of the Aspire pool created post the training. If any region or state does not have a pool they have to go for external recruitment.

Offer & Joining
Process Descriptions:
Once a vacancy is opened up due to resignation or internal movement BHR identifies person in the pool according to the location and current performance.
BHR checks RCU cases with the Zonal RCU Team.
BHR then generates the offer letter with the help of Central HR Team. The candidate has to join the new role in 30 days post hand-over.

Offer & Joining
Before moving to the new role, the existing activities need to be handed over to the replacement.

Process Descriptions:
The below details are captures by each of the before role as a part of the Handover process.
Role FLO:
Biometric Device details,
Group Handover sheet,
NOC by Group etc.
The selected FLO has to move within 45 days.

Role BPM:
MC Assets/ official Documents handover
Cash in Hand Confirmation
PDD/ CLI/ bills/ claims pendency handover
Cash misappropriation declaration etc.
This process needs to be completed within 30 days.

Role FCO:
Biometric Device details
OD Customer Handover Sheet
This process needs to be completed within 60 days.

Role BM:
MC Assets/ official Documents handover
Cash in Hand Confirmation
PDD/ CLI/ bills/ claims pendency handover
Cash misappropriation declaration
Ring Leader and Negative Village list Database etc
This process needs to be completed within 30 days.

Timelines

The Product and Central HR Team completes the process of shortlisting eligible pool within 1st to 6th of every month.
The L&D and the Rural HR Team completes the ASPIRE Assessment Process within 13th to 22nd of every month.
The L&D team completes the Functional and Behavioral Training within 23rd and 27th of the month.
The pool for the new role is identified by the BHR based on the vacancy.

Exception Handling

Any exception to the process defined in the note will need to be approved by Business Head & Business HR Head.

REWARD & RECOGNITION policy

Policy Title
| Reward & Recognition Policy
|
Applicability

This Reward & Recognition Policy aims to recognize and reward performing employees throughout the organisation. We want to not just hire the best talent but retain them too and therefore this policy work towards appreciating and rewarding employees through their tenure with us.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that all policies and processes stipulated in this version shall supersede those set out in any earlier versions of the HR manual. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.

INTRODUCTION

In Meridian Finance, Programs for recognising employees’ achievements are essential for raising staff morale, engagement, and satisfaction in general.

The rewards and recognition program offers a comprehensive collection of employee rewards and recognition programs to ensure that many facets of employee performance and contributions are recognised.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objectives of the policy are as follows:

To recognize exceptional achievements in a systematic manner and to reinforce and institutionalize a culture of meritocracy and positivity.

To communicate a set of behaviors that the organization aims to encourage and that are in pursuance of the mission and vision of the organization and to establish elements of fairness, transparency and enablement in the system of recognition.

Instill a sense of ‘pride of belongingness through contribution’ in every member of the organization.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Respective Rewards & Recognition Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The Company is responsible for ensuring that the Reward & Recognition policy is transparent and communicated well to employees to avoid confusion.
The Company is responsible for reviewing and approving Reward & Recognition process in a timely manner.

Scope
This policy is applicable to all the eligible employees on the rolls of Meridian Finance.

Rewards & Recognitions Categories

3.1 Rising Star Award

3.1.1 Introduction

Rising Star Awards are recognitions given by organizations to acknowledge and celebrate the exceptional contributions and potential of their high-performing employees.
Each business establishes specific performance evaluation criteria, which are used by the business heads to develop a business model. Eligibility for winners in each business is determined based on these models.
This is an individual award category.
3.1.2 Timeline
This takes place from September to October every year.

3.1.3 Eligibility:

Job Band FL IV are eligible for this award category. Please refer Annexure-1 wherein the eligibility is explained with an illustration.

Location:

This reward category is applicable across 6 locations:
Chennai
Chandigarh
Kolkata
Indore
Patna
Bangalore

Form of Rewards:
This reward is awarded to the winners in the following ways:
Trophy
Congratulatory Letter

Process:
Budget Approval:
Budget proposal is made by the CHRO to the MD/CEO for the final approval.

Communication:
BHRs to inform the respective Business Heads regarding the RSA selection process and timelines.

Nomination:
Employees who meet the eligibility criteria set in the business model will be selected.

Evaluation:
Percentage Cap:
There is a specific threshold percentage of employees who will be selected as the winners.
6% of the eligible employees from each business are selected by the Central Lead - HR and Product Head.
The list of the winners and business model are presented to Head BHRs by Central Head, HR and Product Head.

GEC Approval:
The Head BHRs and Business Heads to present the model and winners list to respective GEC member for approval.
After the approval the final list of the winners along with the model is shared with the RSA Core Team.
Please refer Annexure-2 for the Process flow chart.

Result:

The Final list of the awardee is published on the HR portal.

Star Awards

3.2.1 Introduction
STAR Awards are designed to recognize and reward employees who demonstrate exceptional performance, contribute significantly to the company’s goals, or embody the company’s values.
3.2.2 Categories

The eligibility for each reward category is based on the consideration that the rewards will be given in March 2024 as an example.

Bright Spark: Individual reward for new joiners who have gone above and beyond their targets and delivered results.
Eligibility: 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2023.

Pride: Individual reward for Employees who perform exceptionally, aligning their work with the company's core values. They take pride in their contributions, making the organization proud of their achievements.
Eligibility: Before December 2022.

Ambition: Individual reward for Employees who not only achieve their targets but also deliver results that are thought to be impossible.
Eligibility: Before December 2022.

Teamwork: Honoring Teams for Exceptional Project Work.
Eligibility: Team should be cross functional

Transformation Champion: Individual or Team reward for Highest category of rewards and given to consistent exceptional performances.
Eligibility: Chosen during GEC panel discussion

3.2.3 Timeline:

This category of reward is hosted during the last quarter of the Financial year.

3.2.4 Eligibility:
Job Bands FL III and above are eligible.
Employee must have a rating of 3 and above.

3.2.5 Rewards:

This reward is awarded to the winners in the following ways:
Trophy
Congratulatory Letter to Self and/or Family.

3.2.6 Process:
Budget Approval:
Budget proposal is made by the CHRO to the MD/CEO for the final approval.

Nominations:
The nomination form will be updated on the HR portal, where employees can access it.
Employees are eligible to self-nominate or nominate any colleague.

Evaluation:
First Level Due Diligence:
Eligibility verification is conducted for each category based on their respective criteria by Core HR Team
The RCU check is conducted.

Zonal Level Due Diligence:
The names are forwarded to the HR for Zonal Level evaluation.
Further evaluation of the candidates is conducted by the Zonal Head leadership.
The employees are then shortlisted.

Percentage Cap:
There is a specific threshold percentage of employees who will proceed further in the process.
The top employees meeting this criterion are shortlisted for further evaluation.

Formulation of one pager:
BHRs to prepare a profile slide for each shortlisted employee.
The slide will encompass details of the employee's key contributions, business impact and achievements.

Panel Discussion:
The panel includes Business Leaders (BL)
For each individual category, HR POC present each case to the panel.
This discussion period varies, typically lasting up to a week depending on the number of cases.

National Level Due Diligence:
After the panel discussion the candidates are shortlisted.
As per the percentage cap the employees are further shortlisted for the next round.

GEC Panel:
Panel consists of GEC members and MD/CEO
The final selected candidates in each category are presented to the panel.
For team projects, the ones selected by the BL Panel are evaluated.
The final list of awardees is released.

Please refer Annexure, 3 for the Process flow chart.

3.2.7 Result:
The Final list of the awardee is published on the HR portal.

Wall of Fame

3.3.1 Introduction

Wall of Fame typically refers to a display or section dedicated to honoring and celebrating outstanding achievements, accomplishments, or contributions of individuals.
There is an approximate number (417) of employees who has to be honored.
Based on the number of employees in each designation, the number of eligible candidates for the honor is decided. Each winner is given a payout amount, digital and physical certificate for the honor.
The payout amount depends upon the grade and role.

3.3.2 Timeline:

This reward is hosted monthly.

3.3.3 Eligibility:
Each business sets monthly targets, and employees who achieve these targets are selected for the honor.
Employee selection is conducted by the business heads.

3.3.4 Businesses:

Farm Equipment Business
Two-Wheeler Business
Business Operation

Credit

Housing Loans
SME Loans

Payouts Given:

Each Business Head will analyses the monthly targets achieved by employees to determine who will be selected for the Wall of Fame.
HR will send an email to product heads requesting the list of candidates selected for the Wall of Fame.
HR will validate employee details such as active status, name etc. on the HR portal.
Announcement:
Creatives announcing the Wall of Fame winners are sent to each Business Head or POC BHR of each business.
Creatives to be circulated among the team members.
HR will consolidate the list of winning employees from each business and send it to the BHRs.
BHRs will map the payout amounts for the winners and send the list to the HR Operations Team by the 11th of every month.
The HR Operations Team will include the payout amounts for the winners in the upcoming payroll cycle.
HRs to consolidate the winners from all businesses and announce them on the HR portal.
A framed physical winner certificate, along with a winner's email, will be issued to employees across PAN India.
If any winner's name is submitted after the 11th of the month, the payout will be processed in the following month's payroll cycle.

policies.content:
Recruitment Process policy (Frontline)

Policy Title
| Recruitment Process Policy (Frontline & Non-frontline)
|
Applicability
| This is a reference document for the Recruitment Process of Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.
|
Coverage
| Recruitment Process Guidelines and stages covered in the process.
|
Prepared by
|
Team, Compensation & Benefits
|
Reviewed By
| Head, Compensation & Benefits
|
Approved By
| Chief Human Resources Officer
|
Effective date

|
|

This Policy is a reference document for all the internal stakeholders including of Meridian Finance outlining the process and guidelines for the various stages involved in the lateral hiring process.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.

Contents

1.INTRODUCTION 3
1.1 Policy Objective 3
1.2 Policy Management 4
1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation 4
1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates 4
2.Manpower budgeting 4
3.Creating and Publishing Requisition ID 5
4.Candidates Search 5
5.High-volume targeted hiring & Selection 5
6.Interview & Feedback 6
7.Pre-Joining Stage 7
7.1Pre-offer Documentation 7
7.2Pre-offer Background Verification (BGV) documentation 7
8.Creation of Candidate ID 7
9.Role Appreciation Program (RAP) 7
10.Documentation 8
11.Offer Release Process 8
12.Onboarding Process 9

INTRODUCTION

This policy document outlines the standardized framework for recruitment and selection of employees at Meridian Finance, India. It ensures a fair, inclusive, and merit-based approach throughout the hiring process.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objective of the Recruitment Process Policy Manual is to establish a clear and standardized framework for the recruitment and selection of candidates. This policy aims to achieve the following objectives:
Fairness and Transparency: Promote equal opportunities for all candidates based on qualifications, skills, and experience.

Diversity and Inclusion: Actively seek candidates from diverse backgrounds, fostering an inclusive work environment.

Compliance: Adhere to all applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards related to recruitment (e.g., Equal Employment Opportunity, data protection).

Efficiency: Attract and select qualified candidates efficiently, minimizing time-to-fill positions and maximizing the quality of hires.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Recruitment Team is responsible for resolving any questions regarding its interpretation and application. Exceptions to the policy require written approval from the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO).

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates
The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Manpower budgeting

The objective of manpower budgeting within the recruitment process policy is to ensure effective planning and allocation of resources to meet the organization's staffing needs.

Planning and Forecasting: The Recruitment Team, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, will conduct a comprehensive analysis of the organization's manpower requirements. This analysis will consider factors like projected business growth, anticipated attrition, departmental needs, and skill gaps. A manpower budget aligned with the organization's strategic objectives will be developed based on this information.

Resource Allocation: The approved manpower budget will serve as a guideline for allocating resources to different departments and positions. The Recruitment Team will work closely with department heads and hiring managers to ensure efficient resource allocation. Deviations from the budget will require justification and documentation.

Monitoring and Review: The manpower budget will be regularly monitored and reviewed to assess its effectiveness and make necessary adjustments. The Recruitment Team will track actual staffing levels, analyse recruitment and attrition trends, and evaluate the impact of manpower budgeting on organizational performance.

Communication and Transparency: The HR Department will communicate the manpower budgeting process and its outcomes to all relevant stakeholders, including department heads, hiring managers, and employees. This communication will emphasize the importance of manpower budgeting in aligning staffing needs with organizational goals and promoting transparency in resource allocation decisions.

Creating and Publishing Requisition ID
The purpose of creating and publishing a unique Requisition ID within the recruitment process policy is to establish a standardized and efficient system for tracking and managing job vacancies.

Requisition ID Creation: Upon identification of a job vacancy, the hiring manager or designated personnel will create a unique Requisition ID. The ID format should be consistent and include relevant information like department, position title, and creation date to ensure accurate tracking and documentation.

Publishing of Requisition ID: The Requisition ID will be promptly published on the designated recruitment platform or internal job board. It will be accompanied by a comprehensive job description outlining key responsibilities, qualifications, and other pertinent details, ensuring potential candidates have a clear understanding of the position.

Communication and Accessibility: The Recruitment Team will ensure the Requisition ID and associated job details are easily accessible to all relevant stakeholders (hiring managers, recruiters, candidates). A centralized recruitment system or a shared database/portal can be used to achieve this. Clear communication channels will be established to address any queries or clarifications related to the Requisition ID.

Tracking and Documentation: The Recruitment Team will maintain a centralized record of all Requisition IDs and their corresponding job vacancies. This record will include details such as the creation date, status updates, and any changes made throughout the recruitment process. This documentation ensures transparency, accountability, and facilitates reporting and analysis of recruitment activities..
Candidates Search
Sourcing: The Recruitment Team will utilize various sourcing channels to build a strong talent pipeline:

Talent Partners
Career Website/Job portals
Employee Referral Program
Walkins (if applicable)

Eligibility (In case of Micro Loans): To be eligible, candidates must be male graduates between the ages of 21 and 30 and possess a motorcycle and a valid driver’s license.

High-volume targeted hiring & Selection
Bulk Hiring Approach: For high-volume recruitment (e.g., 100 ML Officers), a multi-pronged approach will be used:
Digital Strategy: Social media and strategic job postings will be leveraged to attract a considerable pool of talent.
Additional Sourcing Strategies: The sourcing channels mentioned in Section 4.1 will be used further to strengthen the candidate pool.
.

Interview & Feedback

The purpose of including an interview and feedback clause within the recruitment process policy is to establish a structured and fair process for conducting interviews, evaluating candidates, and providing constructive feedback.

Standardized Interview Process: The Recruitment Team, in collaboration with hiring managers, will develop a standardized interview process tailored to the specific job requirements and aligned with Meridian Finance's organizational values. This process may involve multiple rounds of interviews, such as initial screenings, technical assessments, and final interviews with senior management. All candidates will be informed of the interview process structure beforehand to ensure consistency and fairness.

Interview Panel Composition: A designated interview panel will be assembled for each job vacancy. This panel will consist of relevant stakeholders, typically including the hiring manager, HR representatives, and subject matter experts with specific knowledge and experience relevant to the position being filled. Interview panel members will receive appropriate training on conducting effective interviews, evaluating candidates objectively, and ensuring compliance with legal and ethical guidelines.

Evaluation Criteria: The interview panel will establish clear and objective evaluation criteria based on the essential job requirements and desired competencies outlined in the job description. These criteria will be consistently applied to all candidates throughout the selection process. The panel will assess candidates' qualifications, skills, experience, cultural fit, and any other relevant factors as determined by the specific role.

Feedback Mechanism: Following each interview, the panel will provide timely and constructive feedback to the candidate. This feedback should focus on both strengths and areas for improvement, helping candidates understand their performance and enhance their future job prospects. Feedback will be delivered in a professional and respectful manner, maintaining confidentiality and adhering to all applicable legal requirements.

Documentation and Recordkeeping: The Recruitment Team will maintain accurate and confidential records of all interview assessments and feedback provided to candidates. These records may include interview notes, completed evaluation forms, and any other relevant documentation. This documentation serves to ensure transparency, consistency, and supports informed decision-making throughout the recruitment process.

Communication with Candidates: The Recruitment Team will establish clear communication channels to keep candidates informed about the interview process timeline, including any updates or changes. Candidates will be promptly notified of the outcome of their interview, regardless of whether they are selected to proceed to the next stage. Open and transparent communication helps maintain a positive candidate experience and strengthens the employer brand.
Pre-Joining Stage

Pre-offer Documentation

The Recruitment Team or designated personnel will be responsible for collecting and uploading mandatory pre-offer documents from candidates. These documents will typically include Aadhaar card details and PAN card details, which are essential for further verification processes.

Pre-offer Background Verification (BGV) documentation

Prior to extending an offer, the Recruitment Team will initiate a background verification (BGV) process for shortlisted candidates. This verification typically involves:

Employment Verification: Employment credential checks will be conducted through a reputable third-party vendor, such as the credit information company. To be eligible for employment, candidates must demonstrate a history of positive employment standing, with no record of terminations for cause or instances of abscondment from previous positions.

TRST Score Verification: Verification of the candidate's TRST score may also be included in the BGV process. The TRST score leverages Aadhaar and PAN verification, including linkage status, along with employment verification through provident fund (PF) and Universal Account Number (UAN) details.

The specific details of the BGV process, including the verification methods used, may be subject to change based on internal business needs and compliance with applicable regulations. This policy document serves as a general framework and can be further customized as needed.

Creation of Candidate ID

Purpose

This section outlines the process for assigning a unique identifier (Candidate ID) to each candidate throughout the recruitment process. This ID streamlines tracking, communication, and data management.

Candidate ID Assignment: Upon receiving a candidate application or expression of interest, the Recruitment Team will assign a unique Candidate ID. The ID format should be consistent and systematic to ensure it's:
Unique: No duplicate IDs exist.
Meaningful: It may encode information like year, department, or position type for easy reference

Communication and Confidentiality: The assigned Candidate ID will be promptly communicated to the candidate along with any relevant instructions or next steps. The Recruitment Team is responsible for ensuring the ID is treated as confidential information, shared only with authorized personnel involved in the hiring process.

Tracking and Documentation: A centralized record of all Candidate IDs and their associated candidate information will be maintained by the Recruitment Team. This record should include details like:
Candidate Name
Contact Information
Application Materials
Interview Notes
Assessment Results
Other Relevant Documents

This data facilitates effective communication, accurate tracking, and compliance with data protection regulations.

Retention and Disposal: The Recruitment Team will establish clear policies for retaining and disposing of candidate data and associated Candidate IDs. Candidate data will be retained for a specific period as mandated by legal and regulatory requirements. Once the retention period expires, data will be securely disposed of following applicable data protection guidelines.

Role Appreciation Program (RAP) [Applicable to Micro Loans Only])

Program Overview: The Role Appreciation Program (RAP) is a four-day program designed specifically for onboarding Micro Loan (ML) Officer candidates. It aims to:

Enhance Candidate Experience: Provide an immersive experience to help candidates understand the role and company culture.

Improve Fit: Ensure candidates are well-matched to the position's responsibilities.

Reduce Attrition: Facilitate informed decisions by allowing candidates to assess their suitability for the role

Program Activities: The RAP program is conducted every Wednesday and involves the following key activities:

Day 1:
Classroom training conducted by the Training Manager.
Introduction to the business, its scope, roles, and responsibilities of ML Officers.

Day 2:
Field Visit with senior officers to experience the day-to-day realities of the job.
Opportunity for candidates to assess role alignment with their expectations.
Option to withdraw from the process if there are any concerns. This transparency benefits both parties.

Days 3 & 4:
"PARICHAY" Induction Program: Introduces new employees to the company culture and values.

Documentation

Streamlined Document Collection: This step focuses on gathering and updating essential statutory documents during the onboarding process. For ML recruitment, this typically occurs on the second day of the RAP.

Recruiter/Retainer-Driven Process: To ensure accuracy and efficiency, the assigned Retainer/Recruiter will be responsible for collecting and updating all necessary documentation on the spot. Unlike the Non-Micro Loan recruitment process, candidates do not have the authority to update these details directly on the system.

Real-Time Completion: Documents are completed and collected during the onboarding process itself to minimize delays.
Required Documents (Sample List): Candidates must submit a total of 21 documents for consideration. Some examples include:

Graduation Certificate
Post-Graduation Certificate
Address proof
Declaration Form
PF Nomination Form

Verification and Approval: All entered details and uploaded documents will be verified by the HR Operations Team in real-time. Once approved, the candidate profile will be finalized.

Offer Release Process

Offer Approval: Before extending an offer, relevant stakeholders will review and approve it to ensure:
Alignment with Budget: The offered compensation package fits within the allocated budget for the position.
Compliance with Guidelines: The offer adheres to Meridian Finance's established compensation and benefits guidelines.
Match with Requirements: The offer accurately reflects the position's responsibilities, qualifications, and experience level.

Offer Content: Formal written offers will be presented to shortlisted candidates. These offers will include comprehensive and accurate details about the employment terms, such as:
Position Title: The specific job title being offered.
Compensation and Benefits: A clear breakdown of the salary structure, benefits package, and any applicable allowances.
Start Date: The designated date for commencing employment.
Work Location: The physical location where the employee will be working

Timely Communication and Response: Upon approval, offers will be promptly communicated to candidates through a designated channel, such as email or phone call. Candidates will be given a reasonable timeframe to review the offer and provide their response (acceptance or decline).

Clear Communication Channels: The Recruitment Team will establish clear communication channels to facilitate the offer release process and address any inquiries candidates may have regarding the offer details. This may involve dedicated phone lines, email addresses, or online portals..

Offer Acceptance and Confirmation: Once a candidate accepts the offer, the Recruitment Team will send a written confirmation document. This document will reiterate the key terms of the offer and provide necessary instructions for the onboarding process.

Onboarding Process
New Hire Arrival: On their first day, new hires will report to the designated office location and meet with their pre-assigned reporting manager. The reporting manager will welcome the new employee and provide a brief introduction to the team and work environment.

Data Transmission: The following steps outline the internal data transmission process upon new hire arrival. (Note: This may be specific to Meridian Finance and can be omitted if not relevant):

The reporting manager transmits new hire information/data to the Front-Line Team.
The Front-Line Team then transmits the relevant data to the HR Operations Team.
Upon receiving the data, the HR Operations Team proceeds with creating a PS ID

Continued Onboarding: Following the initial introductions, the HR department will take over the onboarding process. This may involve activities such as:
Completing essential paperwork (e.g., tax forms, benefits enrolment).
Providing new hire orientation programs or training sessions.
Facilitating introductions to colleagues and familiarization with company policies and procedures

This Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) Policy aims to help employees who are not meeting job performance goals. A PIP covers specific areas of performance deficiencies, identifies skills or training gaps and set clear expectation for employees’ future conduct.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that this policy version shall supersede all earlier versions. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.

INTRODUCTION

In Meridian Finance, Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) has a two-pronged approach that's being implemented across different business functions in the organization.

While different businesses choose to implement it at different frequencies as detailed in Annexure 2.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objective of the policy are as follows:

The purpose of the Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) is to help supervisors and direct reports address and resolve performance issues. The PIP communicates the performance discrepancies, when an improved level of performance is to be achieved and the action steps that will assist the employee in meeting performance expectations.

Performance Improvement Plans is implemented to aid in correcting performance challenges associated with the skills and expertise of employees and not be used to correct inappropriate behavioral conduct or a violation of work rules. To address and correct behavioral challenges, disciplinary action, in discussion with BHR, should be undertaken.

PIP process should be undertaken in the spirit of overall enhancement of performance, thereby providing an opportunity to the employee to deliver as per the SMART performance thresholds set for the PIP period.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Respective BHR Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The employer is responsible for ensuring that the Performance Improvement Plan policy is transparent and communicated well to employees to avoid confusion.
The employer is responsible for reviewing and approving Performance Improvement Plan process in a timely manner.

Scope
This policy is applicable to all the eligible employees on the rolls of Meridian Finance and other legal entities under the umbrella.

Policy Guidelines

Only 1 PIP can be issued within a Financial Year for any employee.

If the rating is 3 or above, there has to be a minimum gap of 3 months from the date of Annual Performance Review before PIP is issued. Any extra-ordinary situation may be discussed & mutually agreed under the advice of respective Zonal Business Head and Lead BHR/ Zonal HR head.

PIP Mentor:

Reporting Manager/Any other individual, having a 3 and above as the last rating & 1 grade above, as decided between respective Business HR & Zonal/Regional Business Head, can be a mentor for the PIP process.
Responsibility: To act as guide / support and do regular check-ins.

PIP Targets:

Targets are to be set at the start of the period by the supervisor and approved by Zonal Business Head (OL & above) & Business HR.
A threshold performance has to be finalized with the business to ensure minimum performance levels expected from an employee.
PIP start date will be considered once the approvals are in place.
The employee, who is being placed on PIP will be explained the expected target by his respective superior/s and he/ she will duly sign the document notifying his/ her acceptance of the same.

PIP Review:

PIP will be reviewed jointly between supervisor, employee and Business HR In case the targets have not been achieved as per thresholds on 15th / 30th day.
The corrective actions shall be mentioned and thus the targets/ goals need to be modified accordingly (if required).
A copy of the filled form in all aspects (including all signatures) shall be sent to HR for records.
No further alterations to the targets can be made post this.
Final review shall be done at the end of 45th / 90th day. This shall be the final review and the joint remarks on achievements in light of modified target (applicable, if done during the first review) shall be done. The final form completed in all aspects shall be sent to HR.

PIP Closure:

If the PIP is successfully completed, PIP successful closure mail will be sent by BHR.
In case the PIP is unsuccessful, separation conversation is to be initiated and resignation will be sought from the respective employee.
In case an employee is unwilling to resign, necessary action, including termination of contract, will be initiated by the HR Operations team on advice from the respective BHR.

Non-frontline Employees

Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs): A Path to Improvement

Basis the rating received as an Outcome of the performance appraisal process, the PIP is initiated. If an employee's annual review score falls within a specific range, typically a rating of 2 (indicating performance below expectations), a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) must be initiated. This signifies a need for focused improvement in specific areas.

Collaborative Goal Setting for Improvement

Once the PIP process begins, the BHR head or the employee's reporting manager will schedule a meeting.
For this meeting, the key stakeholders involved will be the employee in consideration, their reporting manager, and the BHR/BHR Head.
During this crucial meeting, all stakeholders will work collaboratively to establish clear, achievable goals tailored to the employee's specific job responsibilities.
These goals should be realistic and directly address the identified performance gaps.

The PIP Process: Dedicated Time for Improvement
The PIP process typically unfolds over a period of 90 days (3 months). This dedicated timeframe allows for focused effort and improvement. Three formal reviews will be conducted throughout the
PIP process, typically on a monthly basis. These reviews assess the employee's progress towards the established goals, identify any challenges they might be facing, and provide ongoing feedback and support. It’s important to note that a fixed start date for the commencement of the PIP process has not yet been established.

Review Schedule: These reviews occur at the end of each month, marking the conclusion of the first (30 days), second (60 days), and third month (90 days).

Rating and Evaluation: Only during the final review (third month) will the employee receive an overall performance rating based on their progress against the established KRAs (Key Result Areas). This rating will be quantifiable, providing a clear metric for assessing their performance during the three-month PIP period. It’s important to note that this rating is solely for the PIP i.e. 3 months and does not affect or change the employee’s original performance rating received after the annual appraisal.

The performance rating received during the PIP is given by the reporting manager; this determines if the employee is retained or not, and the same is communicated to the employee via email or verbally. However, due to the absence of a centralized process/framework this information isn't currently shared with the compensation and benefits team.
PIP Outcomes: Success or Opportunity for Improvement

Success: If the employee achieves a rating of 3 or above in the final review, it signifies successful completion of the PIP, demonstrating significant improvement in performance aligned with the established goals. This leads to their continued employment with the company.
Unsatisfactory Performance: If the employee receives a rating of 2 in the final review, it indicates that the PIP hasn't resulted in the desired improvement. This might lead to termination with a standard 3-month notice period.
Maintaining Performance: Accountability and Follow-Up
If an employee successfully completes a PIP but receives a low rating in the subsequent appraisal review, the BHR head should take account of this performance deviation. This underscores the importance of setting realistic goals, providing ongoing support during the PIP process, and maintaining open communication throughout.

Please refer Annexure-1 to understand the PIP Process summary.

PIP Closure
| BHR in consultation with the Immediate Supervisor
|

Frontline Employees (Incentive-based roles)
Continuous Performance Evaluation in Retail Functions

Retail Functions benefit from a continuous evaluation mechanism due to the abundance of quantifiable data available. This data allows the BHR to assess employee performance from a business perspective on a more frequent basis, typically monthly.

Process Flow

Monthly Performance Evaluation:
Employee performance is evaluated using relevant quantifiable metrics based on pre-determined KRAs (Key Result Areas) specific to their job role.

RAG Rating:
Employees are categorized based on the RAG (Red, Amber and Green) framework.
Red Zone (Needs Improvement): Performance falls below job role requirements (consistently missing targets, poor customer service ratings).
Amber Zone (Opportunity for Improvement): Meets base targets but performance isn't exceptional (improvement opportunities exist).
Green Zone (Meeting Expectations): Consistently meets or exceeds job role expectations.

Performance Improvement Discussion (For Red Zone):

To ensure timely intervention, a performance improvement discussion is initiated if an employee’s performance remains in the Red Zone for three consecutive months.
The first three months serve as an acclimatization period for new employees. During this time, they are not formally evaluated but are provided with support and resources to successfully integrate into their role. Regular feedback discussions may still occur, but a comprehensive performance evaluation starts in month four.
Performance reviews are delivered mid-month, reflecting the previous month's performance. A performance report is provided by the product team to the reporting manager and the BHR. This then informs the decision by the reporting manager and BHR to initiate a PIP for an employee.
BHR, Reporting Manager and employee Discuss performance issues and identify root causes.
A SMART (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time bound) action plan is integrated in the PIP process to create a robust goal framework to ensure that the employee in the next three months (after the performance discussion) is addressing the shortcomings.

Monitoring performance:

Employee's performance is closely monitored in these three months to monitor the progress against the set goals.

Outcomes
Continued Red Zone: After the discussion and failing to achieve goals, further action (up to termination) is taken.
Improvement: Progress towards goals is tracked, and support is provided for continued improvement. If the employee is able to accomplish the set goals and demonstrate productivity, then they are retained.

This policy provides the relevant guidelines and information that governs how Meridian Finance reimburses its employees for business expenses incurred. It also clarifies which business expenses can be claimed for reimbursement. and the documentation required to support the request, and the process for submitting and approving reimbursement claims.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel ‘as mentioned in the Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that this policy version shall supersede all earlier versions. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.

INTRODUCTION

The Business Expenses Reimbursement Policy is designed to enable reimbursement for employees to cover legitimate business expenses incurred towards mobile calling, data usage internet services, meal expenses, etc. This helps to ensure that employees are not financially burdened by work-related expenses and that they are able to carry out their responsibilities effectively. Additionally, these policies promote transparency and consistency in the reimbursement process, ensuring that employees understand the guidelines for submitting reimbursement claims.

1.1 Policy Objective

The overall objectives of the policy are:

The primary objective of these reimbursement policies is to provide appropriate reimbursement to employees for expenses they incur while performing their job duties.
This helps to enhance productivity and efficiency, as employees have the necessary tools and resources to carry out their responsibilities without incurring additional financial burdens.
Establishing clear guidelines for mobile, food, and refreshment reimbursement promotes compliance and transparency within the organization.
By setting maximum reimbursement amounts and defining eligible expenses, organizations can manage their budget and prevent excessive or unnecessary expenses.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Compensation & Benefits Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates
The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The Company is responsible for ensuring that the reimbursement policy is followed consistently. They should provide training and guidance to employees on how to submit reimbursement claims and comply with the policy requirements.
The Company is responsible for reviewing and approving reimbursement claims in a timely manner.
The Company is responsible for monitoring and managing expenses related to mobile and food and refreshment reimbursement. This includes reviewing expense reports, identifying any potential misuse or fraudulent claims, and taking appropriate actions to address such issues.

Mobile Reimbursement

Scope
All permanent employees (FL III & above) of Meridian Finance are eligible for expenses incurred towards mobile usage for official purpose.
General Guidelines

This is applicable only when employees have a postpaid mobile connection for which the bill gets generated in the name of the employee.
The eligibility amount depends on the grade of the employee.
The benefit can be availed for one registered (contact number mentioned in Meridian Finance records) mobile only. In case of change in mobile no, it has to be updated in the record by contacting the HR.
Employee is required to upload Mobile bill on the HR portal under Expense Management.
The SSC team will verify the bill against eligibility and credit the proceeds into the Employee Reimbursement Savings Account.

FAQ, Mobile Reimbursement Policy

Am I eligible to claim Mobile Reimbursement (MR)?
Employees at FL III and above grade are eligible to claim mobile expenses incurred for official purpose. Refer Clause 2.3 above to know your eligibility.

How can I raise mobile reimbursement claim request?
Login to the HR portal, Click on Expense Management > Mobile Reimbursement > New Claim

Against which mobile number should I claim?
You can claim expenses for one registered (contact number mentioned in Meridian Finance records) mobile only. In case of change in mobile no, it must be updated in the record. Contact your Business HR for mobile number change process

How many claim requests can I raise in a month?
You can raise only one claim per month for mobile reimbursement

Can I raise mobile reimbursement claim for prepaid mobile connection?
No. You can claim reimbursement only for postpaid connections

Do I need to send documents to SSC scanning team?
No, you must upload the scanned copy of your mobile bill at the time of raising claim in the HR portal

Which month should I select in “Bill Month” field while raising the claim?
You must select the month as per your bill date. E.g., If bill date is 14th May 2023, May 2023 should be selected as the bill month.

What is my eligibility limit for mobile reimbursement?
Refer clause 2.3 for your monthly eligibility limit

How long it would take for me to get the reimbursement amount post approval of my claim?
Once the claim is approved by the requisite authority, it will be processed and credited to your salary/expense account within 4 working days. UTR no. of such claims will be updated back in the HR portal on next day of payment against your claim request.

How can I view status of my mobile reimbursement claims?
Login to the HR portal, click on Expense Management > Mobile Reimbursement to view the complete details and summary of claims raised.

If I receive an email from SSC that may claim has been put on hold, how can I respond to it and resolve the query?
Click on Mobile Reimbursement (Expense Management) > Select the Request number mentioned in the mail. Respond to the query raised by clicking on “Employee Response”. SSC will process the claim upon receipt of satisfactory response.

The Disciplinary Action Policy provides a set of guidelines for the HR Operations team, Business team, Risk Containment Team, and Business HR Team to follow when addressing instances where an employee fails to adhere to the organization's code of conduct, processes, systems, or engages in actions that could potentially damage the organization's reputation.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy manual should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that all policies and processes stipulated in this version shall supersede those set out in any earlier versions of the HR manual. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.
