INTRODUCTION

The Disciplinary Action Policy, designed to maintain a positive work environment and uphold the organization's values, outlines the process to be followed by various teams within the company when addressing instances of employee misconduct or non-compliance with established guidelines. By clearly defining the roles and responsibilities of different teams involved, such as HR Operations, Business Team, Risk Containment, and Business HR, the policy aims to promote transparency and maintain the organization's reputation. Adherence to this policy helps to foster a culture of professionalism, integrity, and mutual respect among employees.

1.1 Policy Objective

The primary objective of this document is to provide a clear and comprehensive process for the HR team to follow when implementing disciplinary action against an employee who has violated the company's code of conduct, policies, or breached the trust of the organization in any way.

The document emphasizes the importance of upholding the company's code of conduct and policies, which are designed to maintain a positive work environment, protect the interests of the organization, and foster a culture of integrity and professionalism. It highlights the significance of trust and the potential consequences of breaching that trust, emphasizing the need for swift and appropriate action.

1.3 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s HR Operations Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.4 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Scope
This is applicable to all the employees of Meridian Finance and all the legal entities registered under the umbrella.

Process Violation (Discharge/ Termination/ Asked to Leave)

Reviewing the Investigation Report:

Process Description: The investigation report prepared due to violation of process needs to be presented to the Business HR Head and Business Head along with other relevant information and documents that will support the investigation.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the RCU head

Timelines: During bi-weekly meetings

Separation Action to be raised:

Process Description: The Separation Action (Termination / Asked to Leave (ATL) / Discharge) cases along with the execution date to be shared with HR Operations Team.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the RCU team/ BHR

Timelines: After bi-weekly meetings or on request by the Business Team

Validating the PS ID:

Process Description: The employee’s PS ID is validated, and the approvals are taken as per the metrics for separation actions recommended.
Refer Annexure, 1 for the same.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: This is done on receipt of the input.

Preparing the Discharge/Termination letter:

Process Description:
The discharge/termination letter is prepared once all the approvals are received.
The Soft copy of the letter is shared with the BHR to be served to the employee.
The hard copy of the letter available in the HR portal to be delivered to the employee’s residence.
Maintain the registered post acknowledgement copy for records.

Refer Annexure, 2 for the Discharge letter format.
Refer Annexure, 3 for the Termination letter format.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team

Timelines: Within 2 working days from receipt of approval as per metrics.

Steps taken for Asked to Leave (ATL) cases:

Process Description:
In case of ATL, send intimation to Business HR along with the approval mails for execution.
If employee agrees to resign, Business HR to flow normal resignation process.
If employee refuses to resign, Business HR to consult business and get confirmation for Discharge / Termination action.
Get the approval of Business Head and Head, BHR and intimate HR Operations team about the same.
Prepare discharge / termination letter and share with Business HR for execution. The discharge/termination letter is prepared once all the approval are received.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Business HR.

Timelines: This takes place on occurrence.

Issuing Letter:

a. Process Description: The discharge / termination letter will be served to the employee.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Business HR

Timelines: The action is taken by the Business HR as soon as they receive the letter from the HR Ops team.

Employee Separation:

Process Description:
The employee separation is being executed in the the HR portal.
Navigation steps: the HR portal > Workforce Management > Separation > Initiate Termination Process > Search PS ID > Termination Date > Select the Reason > Select the Reason2 > Mention additional Remarks > Submit.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: This takes place on the date of serving the letter.

Capturing details:

Process Description:
Capture the details of the case including the date of separation in the Disciplinary MIS.
Refer, Annexure 4 for Disciplinary MIS Format.
Lists of separated employees to be shared with F&F team.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: This is an on-going process.

Reporting to the Central HR Team:

a. Process Description: Sharing the MIS disciplinary actions with the Central HR Team.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Business HR

Timelines: The action is taken on the 10th of subsequent month.

Refer Annexure 9 to understand the Process flow in this case.

Process Description for Unauthorised Absence (Absconding)

Update the the HR portal:

a. Process Description: Mark employee as “Absconding” in the HR portal system, when employee is on unauthorized absence from duties for 5 consecutive working days.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Immediate Supervisor of employee or the Business HR.

Timelines: After unauthorized absence of 5 working days.

Approval of Absconding request:

Process Description:
The Absconding request needs to be approved in the the HR portal.
The navigation steps are - Login to the HR portal, Change the role to ‘Disciplinary Action’ > Workforce Management > Separation > Approve Absconding Process > Search PS ID > Approve Request

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: Within 1 working day from time of receipt of input.

For Unreported cases:

Process Description:
In cases where employee has not reported for more than 5 working days and not completed 30 days from the date of joining, Abandonment of contract action to be executed in the HR portal.
No Abandonment of contract letter to be send to the employee.
Lists of separated employees to be shared with F&F team.

Navigation: Login to the HR portal > Workforce Management > Separation > Exit Initiate > Search PS ID > Last working date > Save

In cases where employee has not reported for more than 5 working days and completed 30 days from the date of joining, Initial warning letter to be sent to employee’s residential address available in the HR portal through Registered Post.
Refer, Annexure 5 for Warning Letter Format.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: This is done within 1 working day from approval of absconding.

In case of Employee Reporting back:

Process Description:
If employee reports back to duty, Business HR to intimate HR Operations team for necessary action.
HR Operations team to revoke the “Absconding” action in the HR portal and update Business HR about the revocation through mail.
Navigation - Login to the HR portal > Workforce Management > Separation > Exit Initiate / Revoke > Search PS ID > Revoke date > Remarks > Save.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team and Business HR.

Timelines: Within 24 hours from receiving input.

In case of No response from the employee:

Process Description: In case there is no response from employee to the initial letter sent / non receipt of any input for revocation of absconding action from the Business HR for 5 working days from the date of warning letter sent.
Abandonment of contract letter to be prepared and sent to the employee.
Refer, Annexure 6 for Abandonment of Contract Letter Format
Abandonment of contract action to be executed in the HR portal.
Navigation - Login to the HR portal > Workforce Management > Separation > Exit Initiate / Revoke > Search PS ID > Separation date > Save.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: Post 5 working days from date of dispatch of initial warning letter.

Maintaining Records:

a. Process Description: •Maintain proper records of all warning letters and abandonment of contract letters sent to employees through registered post.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: This is an on-going process.

Updating F&F team and Payroll team:

a. Process Description:
Share lists of separated employees with F&F team
Share consolidated list of all separation cases with Payroll team for the credit information company reporting.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team

Timelines:
The list is shared with the F&F team within 24 hours from the date of execution.
The consolidated list is shared with the payroll team on the 10th of every month.

Refer Annexure 10 to understand the Process flow in this case.

Process Violation (Warning Letters)

Investigation

Process Description: Detail Investigation is to be conducted in matters of indiscipline/ process violation/ misconduct.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the RCU team and Business HR.

Timelines: This is an on-going process.

Identify the impact on business activity:
Process Description: Recommend “warning” against employee by identifying the impact of action on business activity / field, financial / reputational damages to organization.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Regional RCU team and Zonal HR.

Timelines: This is an on-going process.

Creating letter:
Process Description:
Prepare warning letter capturing the non-compliance / process violation and share soft copy of the letter with the BHR. Refer, Annexure 7 for Warning Letter Draft.
Capture the details of the case in the MIS tracker. Refer, Annexure 8 for Warning Letter MIS Format.

Responsibility: This activity is taken up by the Disciplinary Team.

Timelines: This is done within 2 days from receipt of input.

Issuing the Letter:

Process Description: After the warning letter is created it is being issued to the employees by the Business HR.

Responsibility: This is done by the BHR

Timelines: This is issued by the BHR as soon as they receive the letter from the HR Ops team

INTRODUCTION

The Company believes that a successful onboarding process is crucial for new employees to integrate smoothly into the company culture, understand their roles and responsibilities, and feel supported from day one. This policy document serves as a comprehensive resource to help HRs and the internal stakeholders of the company to navigate through the onboarding process and make a seamless transition for the new hires.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objective of this policy is to ensure a smooth and efficient onboarding process for new employees at Meridian Finance. By following this policy, we aim to provide a positive experience for new hires and ensure that all necessary steps are taken to verify their profile, documents, and generate employee IDs.

This document ensures that Employee IDs (PS IDs) of new joiners are generated by the HR Operations Team, only post verifying the completeness of Employee Profile and documents of the candidate on the HR portal.

1.2 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s HR Operations (Onboarding) Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.3 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Scope
This is applicable to all the employees of Meridian Finance and all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Process Flow
The onboarding process for different job grades are described in this document.

Refer Annexure, 5 to understand the Process flow for On-boarding process that is carried out for FL III & above. Refer Annexure, 6 to understand the Process flow for On-boarding process that is carried out for FL IV.

Stage 1, Verifying Post Offer documents for FL III & above.

Process Description

The process for verification of Candidate Profile and Document is different for grade ‘FL IV’ and ‘FL III & Above’.

For FL III & above, Documents are available for verification under header “Verify post offer documents”.
Profiles are available for verification under header “Verify candidate profile”.

For FL IV, Profiles and Documents are available under single header “Verify candidate profile”.

For checking documents of FL III & Above candidates, select “Verify Post Offer Documents.”

Steps to be followed are, Go to header ‘Action’ and click on link ‘Verify’ to check the documents mentioned in Annexure, 1

In case of document discrepancy for FL III & above,
Resend to Candidate and BHR
The Discrepancy needs to be cleared by the candidate and re-submitted for HR Ops necessary action.

Refer Annexure 1 for details.

Responsibility:

The responsibility of this stage lies with the On-boarding team.

Timelines

The step mentioned in clause 4.1(2) should be completed 7 days prior to Date of Joining.
The step mentioned in clause 4.1(3) should be completed at the time of document verification.

Stage 2 - Approval of Candidate Profile for FL III & above

Process Description

The onboarding team has to follow the below steps to approve the candidate’s profile:
In the HR portal, under Talent Acquisition tab, select appointment.
Then click on “Approve Candidate Profile” tab for verifying the profile of the candidates whose documents have been verified.

Under candidates’ profile, verify the following sections:
Photo: Passport size for ID card Creation
Personal Info: DOB/Name/ Blood Group/ Personal email id
Contact Address: As per the address proof
Education: As per document proof
Bank Info: As per bank document Proof
Previous Employment: As per resume & resignation letter proof
Identification Details: PAN & Aadhar

Refer Annexure 2 for details.

In case of profile discrepancy for FL III & above,
Resend to Candidate and BHR mentioning proper reason for rejection.
The Discrepancy needs to be cleared by the candidate and re-submitted for HR Ops necessary action.

Responsibility:

The responsibility of this stage lies with the On-boarding team.

Timelines

The step mentioned in clause 4.1(1) should be done immediately after the documents are approved.
The step mentioned in clause 4.1(2) should be completed once the profile is submitted by the candidate.
The step mentioned in clause 4.1(3) should be completed at the time of candidate profile verification.

Stage 3, Approval of Candidate profile and documents, FL IV

Process Steps

Verify documents as per mandatory documents check list.

Verify Candidate profile as below:
Photo: Passport size for ID card Creation
Personal Info: DOB/Name/ Blood Group/ Personal email id
Contact Address: As per the address proof
Education: As per document proof
Bank Info: As per bank document Proof
Previous Employment: As per resume & resignation letter proof
Identification Details: PAN & Aadhar

Refer Annexure 3 for details.

In case of profile or documents discrepancy for FL IV,
Resend to Frontline HR Team.
The Discrepancy needs to be cleared by the Frontline HR team and re-submitted to the HR Ops team for necessary action.

Refer Annexure 3 for details.

Responsibility:

The responsibility of this stage lies with the On-boarding team.

Timelines

The above process is completed at the time of profile and document verification step conducted for FL IV.

Stage 4, Employee ID Creation
Process Steps

Confirming the Date of Joining (DOJ):
Once profile and documents are approved, the detail of candidate starts reflecting in Confirm/ Update DOJ
For FL III & Above: BHR confirms the joining date.
For FL IV: Immediate supervisor (IS) of the candidate confirms the joining date.
For updating DOJ, go to
Talent Acquisition > Appointment > Confirm/ Update Date of Joining
MIS on the status of on-boarding with the current stage is available in
Talent Acquisition > Pre-joining >Analytics Studio > Recruitment Tracker - TAT

Employee Code Generation:

Once DOJ is confirmed in the HR portal, the below steps needs to be completed for employee code generation:

Go to Appointment > Appointment > Click on Appoint under header ‘Action’.
In Appointment, click on “Appoint” and check the below fields:
Duplication Check
Organization Info like-
Legal entity
Business Unit
Organization Unit
Grade
Reporting manager etc.
Refer Annexure 4 for details.

Click on “Append Workforce” to generate the Employee Code

Responsibility:

The responsibility of this stage w.r.t Confirmation of the DOJ lies with the BHR and IS team.
The responsibility w.r.t Employee code generation lies with the On-boarding team.
Stage 5, Updating personal profile in the HR portal.

Process Steps

The existing employees have to initiate updating of Personal information in ‘the HR portal’ by following the below steps:
In Workforce Management > Click on ‘Update Profile’ and update relevant sections.

The HR Ops team will be verifying the detail along with the documents once the profile is updated by the employee.

Below are few of the areas given for reference which needs to be updated by the employees while updating the Employee Profile.

Updating Bank Info details:
Click on ‘Bank Info’ tab under ‘Update Profile’, employee updates their bank account details.
i.e. IFSC Code, account number and account name.
Verify bank info details as per the proof provided i.e. passbook front page/ cancelled cheque copy/ online statement. The document proof should have the name of the account holder, account number and IFSC code.
If the cheque leaf does not display the account holder's name, then scan copy of 1st page of passbook / online statement with all above details mandatorily required.

Updating Identification details:
In Identification details, employee updates their PAN / Aadhar/ UAN and uploads the supporting documents along with it.
Check whether PAN & Aadhar number is as per the proof provided.
Aadhar number should be 12 digits
In PAN 4th character should be “P”

Updating Qualification details:
In Qualification tab, employees update their qualification details & upload the supporting documents under the header ‘Upload Document’.
Check whether the education details like year of passing, university name & Course name is as per education certificates/ marksheet.

This Equal Employment Opportunity Policy ensures that all employees and potential employees are treated equitably and fairly regardless their race, gender, caste, statutes in society or disability.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy manual should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that all policies and processes stipulated in this version shall supersede those set out in any earlier versions of the HR manual. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.

INTRODUCTION

Meridian Finance is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and upholding fairness in terms of recruitment, promotion & pay. This policy elucidates our commitment to promote equality and conduct our business in accordance with the principles of social justice, including but not limited to Access, Equity, Diversity, Participation, and Human Rights. Meridian Finance is committed to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment and shall take all reasonable steps to recruit and promote employees based on merit and capability.

1.1 Policy Objective

The Company is deeply committed to fostering an environment where all its employees and job applicants are treated equitably and with the utmost respect. This Policy embodies the Company's unwavering dedication to advancing equality while conducting business in accordance with principles of social justice, respect, and the freedom to express oneself. The primary aim of this policy is to prevent discrimination based on their gender, sexual orientation, religion, race, ethnicity, disability, or any other unique attribute.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s HR team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made, the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The company’s responsibilities with regards to this policy includes:

Non-Discrimination: Ensuring fair treatment without bias based on protected characteristics.

Accessibility: Providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities.

Training and Education: Promoting awareness and understanding of equal opportunity principles.

Complaint Handling: Establishing a fair process for addressing discrimination complaints.

Monitoring and Compliance: Regularly evaluating practices to ensure compliance with laws.

Accountability: Holding employees accountable for violating the policy.

Scope
This policy covers all employees and value chain members with disabilities. They could be job applicants, full time / part time employees applies to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, learning and development, working conditions, pay and career progression.

This Equal Employment Opportunity Policy applies to all employees and value chain members, who are vulnerable to discriminatory treatment due to certain individual characteristics. This Equal Employment Opportunity policy is in accordance with the provisions of The Right of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 and Central Government Rules 2017. We will always abide by the principles of the Policy in letter and in spirit.

Terms of Employment Opportunities

The selection of new staff will be based on the job requirements and the individual suitability and ability to do, or to be trained for the job. Person specifications and job descriptions will be limited to those requirements that are necessary for the effective performance of the job. Candidates for employment, promotion or transfer will be assessed objectively against the requirements for the job.

The company will strictly refrain from demonstrating bias or prejudice towards individual differences which will be valued and protected. Employees are entitled to work in a discrimination free where their worth and rights are respected.

Discrimination in any form is strictly prohibited, and we clearly define the consequences for such behavior. We are dedicated to ensuring that no form of discrimination hinders the professional of any employee.

Facilities and Amenities:

We prioritize the well-being and rights of all such employees/individuals who are vulnerable. We ensure the confidentiality of employees' personal information in line with relevant data privacy laws and provide necessary infrastructure facilities, security measures, and amenities to support the effective performance of all employees.

We will strive to ensure that our physical infrastructure, facilities, communication and information technology systems are accessible to all employees including employees with disabilities. Our Corporate Head Office is accessible to person with disabilities, and we will ensure to make other offices inclusive in due course of time.

Recruitment and Career Progression:

All positions are open to all people and are published on the career page and job portals.

We encourage all candidates with different disabilities to apply. Our decision of employment, career progression, training or any other benefits are solely based on merit. We follow an inclusive evaluation process by ensuring that a person with disability is provided with any suitable flexibility and accommodations that may be required so that she / he may be evaluated fairly. Company will identify posts / vacancies that would be suitable for disabled persons.

All terms of employment, benefits, facilities and services will be reviewed from time to time in order to ensure that there is no unlawful direct or indirect discrimination because of one or more of the protected characteristics.

Accommodation and Leaves:

Actions aiming towards equal opportunity include the following.

Use of inclusive, diversity-sensitive language in all official document, signs etc.
Modification of structures and facilities to accommodate people with disabilities.
Leave and flexible work arrangements policies to provide for parental, medical or other needs.
Hiring, Training and evaluating processes that do not focus on characteristics irrelevant to employment, job specifications, qualifications, productivity etc.
Inclusions of religious and national holidays of all people that are part of the workforce in the company’s official schedule and arrange their leaves upon request.
Education sessions and groups on diversity for employees.
Open door practice to make the reporting of unlawful discriminatory conduct easier.
Active engagement of employees to propose improvements.
Explicit prohibition of discrimination and clearly defined consequences.

Equal pay and equality of terms:

The company is committed to equal pay and equality of terms in employment. It believes all employees should receive equal pay where they are carrying out like work, work related as equivalent or work of equal value. In order to achieve this, the Company will endeavor to maintain a pay system that is transparent, free from bias and based on objective criteria.

Grievance Procedure:

All supervisors and managers are responsible to ensure that policies of equal opportunities are applied at all times and that all procedures and practices are free of discrimination. All staff are obliged to follow legal guidelines and equal opportunity employer principles. In case when these rules are violated, employees can address the offender directly. If the issue is not resolved, they can report to Human Resources Department or their immediate supervisor. The report will be investigated as soon as possible, and all parties will be listened to. The employee that suffered the offence will be protected against harassment and victimization.

Liaison Officer:

Company has appointed Mr. Debashis Sharma, Chief Manager, Human Resources as Liaison Officer who shall oversee the recruitment of disabled persons and make necessary provisions and ensure facilities for such employees in the establishment. He can be reached at 7045592668 and his email id is debashissharma@meridianfinance.com.

Maintenance of Records:

Company maintains below records reflecting details of the disabled persons employed.

No. of persons with disabilities employed and the date from which employed.
Name, gender and address of the persons with disabilities.
Nature of disability of such persons.
Nature of work rendered by such disable person.
Kind of facilities provided to persons with disabilities.

Monitoring Equal Opportunity:

The company will regularly monitor the effects of selection decisions and personnel practices and procedures in order to assess whether equal opportunity is being achieved. If changes are required, the Company will implement them.

Administration of the Policy:

The Human Resources Department is responsible for the administration, tracking, and communication of this Policy. They are also available to address any questions or concerns that may arise. In addition, all levels of management will actively support the implementation of this Policy within their respective departments, fostering a culture that values compliance with this policy.

Breach of Policy:

We reserve the right to take appropriate disciplinary or legal action when deemed necessary in response to reported violations of this policy. Anyone found to be harming, injuring, or endangering the life, safety, health, or well-being, whether mental or physical, of any vulnerable employee/individual. through acts such as physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse, or economic abuse will be subject to legal consequences in accordance with applicable laws. This Policy document is made available with the clear objective of establishing a standard approach for addressing the issues discussed herein, with a focus on inclusivity and equal treatment for all employees.

This policy details the support provided by the Company during such movements including Transportation, boarding and lodging and resettlement expenses.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in Clause 1.2.1.

INTRODUCTION

In Meridian Finance, the transfer of eligible employees is treated consistently and fairly when considering movement within the organization. Meridian Finance provides ample opportunities to employees for their career development.

1.1 Policy Objective

The overall objectives of the policy are:

It helps to improve the working experience of the employees as they get to work with different people and different environments.
It provides a new sense of motivation and satisfaction as transfer is growth-oriented opportunity for the employees.
It helps to ensure overall skill development of the employees within the organization.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Compensation & Benefits Team & the respective BHR SPOCs will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The Company is responsible for ensuring that the transfer policy is transparent and communicated well to employees to avoid confusion about who should be transferred when and on what basis.
The Company is responsible for reviewing and approving transfer in a timely manner.
The Company is responsible to indicate in clear terms and conditions of the transfer. There should not be any scope for ambiguity.

Definition

An employee, when transferred from one city to another on account of business requirement, is reimbursed for all direct expenses incurred due to relocation.

Scope
This policy is applicable to all the on the roll employees of Meridian Finance.

Exception
In case of transfer initiated at the request of the employee, the policy stands void.
Relocation Reimbursement & Support Guidelines

Relocation Travel Support

The mode of one-time travel arrangement of the employee to the new location at the time of transfer will be managed by the Facilities and Channel Management (FCM) Team.
Incase the employee requests the travel arrangements for any of his/her family members, then he/she is supposed to route the same through the BHR along with the approval from his Immediate Supervisor requesting the same.
The BHR then gets hold of the final approval from the Head BHR. Only on the basis of such approval, the FCM team arranges travel for the employee’s family members.

Transportation of Baggage, Packing, Loading and Unloading

The company will provide support to the employees with transportation, packing, loading and unloading of household goods at the time of relocation.
The limit for extending this benefit is defined by the distance between the current city and the city after relocation as per the Job grades.
The company shall also reimburse the cost of moving vehicles based on the Job grades.
Employee who is relocated shall be provided with Transit Insurance depending on the grade.
Please refer Annexure 1 for the above reimbursement limits.

Clawback clause in case of employee exit

If an employee leaves or resigns from the services of the Company within one year of from the date of joining/effective date of transfer and has already claimed relocation expenses, the employee would be required to refund the full amount claimed.

Boarding and Lodging

Employee who is relocated shall be reimbursed for expenses incurred for the lodging and boarding or will be entirely managed by the FCM Team depending on the grade and distance between current city & city after resettlement.

The employees will be provided with the accommodation facility for a period of 7 (Seven) Days in the new location.

In case of any request for extending the accommodation beyond 7 days, the employee needs to route the same through his/her BHR with appropriate reason to get final approval from the Head BHR.
Accompanying Family Expenses, The Expenses of spouse and any children will be covered by the company if they accompany the employee during the relocation. Spouse expense limits would be the same as that of the employee for travel, accommodation and meals. Children’s cost for accommodation and meals will be ½ of the entitlement of the employee, for travel it will be the same as the employee.

Resettlement Expenses-

At the time of relocation, employees are reimbursed with one month’s Brokerage & charges on Stamp.
Duty & Registration (10% of Leave & License Agreement), depending on the city relocated to and grade of the employee. Resettlement expense is a one-time ad hoc payment made to an employee.

Please refer Annexure, 2 for the limits defined for one time re-settlement expenses.
For Relocation of vehicle and Household goods:

Employee will be asked to submit 03 quotations.
Minimum of the 03 quotations received will be approved subject to maximum limit cap as per the eligibility matrix below.

Guidelines on cases, more than one transfer in a financial year
In such cases where the employee is transferred/relocated more than once in a financial year, then the BHRs need to get the written approval from BHR Head and the CHRO prior to initiating the transfer.
For such approved cases, the clawback recovery applies only to the latest transfer expenses given, one year period will be looked at from the effective date of latest transfer.

INTRODUCTION

In Meridian Finance, Shuttle Service is to provide efficient solutions to employee’s transportation. We endeavour to provide the best possible shuttle service to our employees. We place the safety and responsibility of the employees as our highest priority.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objective of this policy is to ensure safe, affordable, quick, comfortable, reliable and sustainable access for last mile connectivity for employees to travel to office and back.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from 16th May, 2024

The Company’s respective BHR & FCM team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Scope & Coverage
This policy applies to all colleagues on the payroll of Meridian Finance based at Kalina and Mahape Offices in Mumbai, however this service does not apply to employees who have opted for the EOCS or COCS policy.

Sticker Issuance
Employees who wish to avail the shuttle service must obtain a color-coded sticker specific to their preferred shuttle.

The stickers should be affixed to their I-Cards.

Stickers will be issued to eligible employees who have expressed interest in the service.

Please refer to Annexure 1 for the locations where stickers will be issued

Guidelines regarding Boarding & Security
The company prioritizes the safety and security of employees using the shuttle service.

Employees with the appropriate sticker will be allowed to board the corresponding shuttle service.

It is expected that employees maintain decorum and discipline while using the shuttle service and not to overcrowd the bus beyond seating capacity.

As per RTO laws and regulations, passengers standing in the private bus while travelling is prohibited. Hence the passengers boarding the shuttle should follow the instructions and directions of the bus driver and obey the RTO laws. RTO or police in charge could charge a significant amount of fees from the Bus contractor in case of violation of the stated rule and regulations.

Any suspicious or unsafe behavior should be reported immediately to your HR SPOC/FCM SPOC. .

Shuttle Availability
The size of the shuttle buses is determined by the prevailing traffic conditions at the railway station.

The shuttle service operates on a "first come, first served" basis.

Reserving seats for oneself or others is not permitted.

Buses will depart according to the time-table mentioned in Annexure 2 or when the bus is fully occupied, whichever comes first.

In case of changes to the time-table due to traffic conditions, employees will be notified at least a week in advance.

Employees should not delay the departure of the bus for any reason.

Guidelines on Queuing & Departures:

Employees are not allowed to queue up for the bus before the end of office hours (6:30 PM).

While the shuttle service is provided free of charge, employees are not obligated to use it.

The company's time and attendance policy apply uniformly to all employees, regardless of their use of the shuttle service. No exceptions will be made for late-coming due to the shuttle not reaching the office on time.

Loss or Damaged Stickers:

In case of lost or damaged stickers, employees should report the issue to the designated department for a replacement.

A fee may be charged for replacement stickers, as determined by the company.

Feedback and Suggestions:
The company welcomes feedback and suggestions from employees regarding the shuttle service.

Employees are encouraged to provide feedback on the service quality, routes, stops, or any other relevant aspect.

Feedback can be submitted through the designated channels or to the responsible department through their respective HR SPOC.

Termination or Suspension of Services:

The company reserves the right to terminate or suspend the shuttle service at any time, based on operational requirements or other factors.

In such cases, employees will be notified in advance, and alternative transportation arrangements may be provided if feasible.

This Policy document includes guidelines and procedures to ensure fair and effective recruitment processes to avoid any conflict of interests. These policies are designed to attract and select the most qualified candidates while promoting diversity, equal opportunity, and compliance with legal requirements.

Any questions and suggestions on the implementation of the policy should be directed to the ‘Authorized Personnel’ as mentioned in Clause 1.2.1.

For the purpose of this document, the term ‘company’ would refer to Meridian Finance & all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Please note that this policy version shall supersede all earlier versions. Meridian Finance will endeavour to update this policy as required.

Contents

INTRODUCTION

In order to maintain fairness, transparency, and avoid potential conflicts of interest, Meridian Finance have designed this policy regarding the hiring of relatives. This policy typically outlines guidelines and restrictions to ensure that the recruitment process remains unbiased and is based solely on merit.

1.1 Policy Objective

This policy aims to uphold the principles of equal opportunity and prevent favouritism or nepotism within the organization. By implementing this policy, the company strives to create a level playing field for all candidates and maintain a professional and impartial work environment.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Business HR Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Scope
All employees of Meridian Finance are covered by this policy.

Definition of Relative
For the purpose of this policy, the term “relatives” are defined as under:
a person connected by blood up to a third degree or by marriage or by adoption.
Direct relatives (First Degree) such as spouse, brother, sister, father, mother
Second-degree relatives include an individual's grandparents, grandchildren, uncles, aunts, nephews, nieces, and half-siblings.
Third-degree relatives include an individual's great - grandparents, great grandchildren, great uncles/aunts, and first cousins.

General Policy Guidelines
Hiring of any relatives of Whole Time Directors shall conform with the provisions of the Companies Act. Hiring of relatives of Whole Time Directors and KMPs (covers MD, ED, CFO and Company Secretary) will require the specific permission of the Board of Directors.
Hiring of Relatives of Members of Executive Committee and Leadership Team will require the approval of the CEO & MD.
Hiring of any relatives of all other employees other than those mentioned in point No 1 and 2 above, will be allowed if the posting of the candidate is not in the same business unit as of the referring employee. Placements shall not be made where one employee is in a position to supervise or influence the related employee's increments or promotion of the employee, or the granting of any benefits, or where the handling of certain information can create awkward work situations. The employee related to the prospective candidate shall not be involved in the selection process. Such candidates will not be included for the rewards in an employee referral scheme. Canvassing of any type for the hiring of such candidate will go negatively for the candidate in the selection decision. The hiring of such candidate will be purely on merit and the business need for the vacancy.
No employee shall use his/her position or influence directly or indirectly to secure employment for any person related, whether by blood or marriage or by adoption to the employee or to the employee's wife or husband, whether such a person is dependent on the employee or not.
In case of marriage between employees in the same company, it shall be ensured that the employees concerned shall be posted in different departments/businesses in order to ensure that there is no conflict of interest or an awkward work situation.
It may so happen that an employee is unaware of the recruitment of a second degree or third degree relative being hired in the company. Such non-disclosure shall not be treated as violation of the CoC (Code of Conduct) unless there is a complaint or objection raised from any quarter about such hiring and there is evidence to prove that the employee had a direct or indirect influence on such hiring. In such cases, concealment of such material information by the employee concerned will be treated as a violation of the CoC.
Roles and Responsibilities
For Employees

It shall be the responsibility of every employee who is related to a selected candidate or if the selected candidate is connected with a related party (customer, vendor, competitor) selected for a job role to intimate the HR Department concerned about the nature of relationship with the candidate, that he/she was not involved in or in influencing the selection decision and that he/she shall not canvas for the candidate in the future for the career progress of the candidate. Such intimation will be in the interest of transparency and will be taken on record. Such procedure will be followed even where the candidate has been referred by an employee under an employee referral scheme, for an advertised/pre- announced vacancy and the Company has hired the candidate based on merit and the referee is not involved in any way with the hiring process.

Since this is a new policy, where necessary, existing employees in addition to all new hires, if related to any employee/director/customer/vendor/competitor in the organization will need to submit a self - declaration to the respective HR Department.

For Candidates
Disclosure by a candidate in the Employment Application Form about being related to any employee in the Company is compulsory. Failure to do so will disqualify the candidature of the candidate or if discovered later will call for an explanation by the candidate and the employee concerned, with consequences to follow, since such failure to disclose shall be seen as concealment of material information. Such disclosure by a candidate in the Employment Application Form about being related to an employee will be an essential but not sufficient step in fulfilling the requirements of this policy.

INTRODUCTION

The Company believes that a renewal of contract & revision of salary is crucial for Retainers / Consultants to integrate smoothly into the company culture. This policy document serves as a comprehensive resource to help HRs and the internal stakeholders of the company to navigate through the renewal & salary revision process for Retainers / Consultants.

1.1 Policy Objective

This policy aims to provide clear guidelines for the renewal of contracts and the revision of salaries for Retainers/Consultants at Meridian Finance (Meridian Finance). The objective is to ensure a transparent and consistent process for managing the contractual agreements and compensation of these individuals. It establishes a framework for evaluating and adjusting compensation at the time of renewing the contracts of the retainers and the consultants.

1.2 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s HR Operations Team and the respective BHRs will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.3 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.4 Policy Review and Compliance

All BHRs, HR Operations team members, and relevant stakeholders are responsible for complying with this policy.
This policy will be reviewed periodically to ensure its effectiveness and alignment with organizational requirements.

Scope
This is applicable to all the Retainers and Consultants of Meridian Finance and all registered legal entities under the umbrella.

Process Flow
The below guidelines ensure a systematic and transparent process for contract renewal and salary revision for Retainers/Consultants at Meridian Finance. By following these steps, Meridian Finance aims to maintain consistency and fairness in managing contractual agreements and compensation for these individuals.

3.1 Contract Expiry Notification Process
The HR Operations Team Member is responsible for informing the respective Business HR Representatives (BHRs) about the upcoming contract expiration.
This notification should be sent two months prior to the contract end date.
A draft email template for this notification is provided in Annexure-1.
Additionally, a reminder should be sent one week after the original advice. E.g., If the contract end date is any date in the month of Sep 2022, then the communication will be sent on 1st week of July 2022. Refer Annexure 1 for the format.

3.2 Zonal Head Concurrence for Contract Renewal
The Zonal Business HR is responsible for obtaining the concurrence of the Zonal Head (of the respective Business Unit) for the renewal of the contract.
This concurrence should be obtained within 15 days of the first reminder sent by the HR Operations Team.
3.3 Salary Increase Evaluation
Upon receiving the advice for contract extension from the respective Zonal HR Head, the BHR should assess if there is a need for a salary increase.
The salary increase should be based on the average increment for the immediately preceding increment cycle for the respective Business Unit.

3.4 Approval for Salary Increase
If a salary increase is required, the Lead BHR should seek approvals from the RCU Head and the BHR Head upon receiving the contract extension approval from the Zonal HR.

3.5 Approval for Above-Average Salary Increase
If the proposed salary increase is above the average increment, the Head BHR should obtain written approval from the CHRO (Chief Human Resources Officer) along with justifications upon receiving the extension approval from the Zonal HR.

3.6 Sharing Approval Details with HR Operations
Once approval is received from the CHRO/RCU Head and BHR/Head, the Zonal BHR should share the approval details with the HR Operations team along with the relevant approval emails.

3.7 Preparation of Revised Contract Letter
Based on the inputs received from the Zonal BHR, the HR Operations team member is responsible for preparing the revised contract letter. This letter should be shared with the respective Zonal BHR.

3.8 Contract Letter Distribution and Acknowledgement
After the HR Operations team prepares the contract letter, the Zonal BHR should share the letter with the respective Retainer/Consultant.
The Retainer/Consultant should sign an acknowledgement copy of the letter before the end of the preceding month of the initial contract completion date.

3.9 Updating Records
Upon receiving the signed acknowledgement copy from the Zonal BHR, HR Operations should update the records accordingly.

INTRODUCTION

Petty Cash funds are small amounts of cash kept on hand for the purpose of making small purchases, reimbursing employees for out-of-pocket expenses, and other miscellaneous expenses.

In Meridian Finance, the Board of Management approve the use of petty cash system. This document will lay out the controls and limits around the use of petty cash.

1.1 Policy Objective

The purpose of the Policy is to establish guidelines for the use of petty cash advances. Petty cash advances are intended for incurring expenses that are of low value and need to be paid in cash. In situations where it is not possible or practical to make payments through the vendor payable application, petty cash can be used as an alternative method of payment. This helps to ensure that petty cash is used appropriately and in accordance with the organization's financial policies and procedures.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s FCM (Facilities of Channel & Management) team and the F & A Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Scope
This policy applies to all permanent employees of Meridian Finance and all other legal entities registered under the umbrella.

Eligibility to advance Petty Cash

The following designated employees will be eligible for advance against petty cash expenses:

Head Office: Designated employee from FCM Team.

Branches: Designated employee from the Branch Operation Team, if available, else, the designated senior most branch employee.

Meeting Centers: Designated Meeting Center Manager (MCM).

The above employees shall be designated by Group Head FCM / Head Facilities in case of HO and branches and by Product Manager (ML0) in case of Meeting Center.

Entitlements:
Location
| Amount in (INR)
|
HO
| 50,000
|
Branches
| 7,500
|
Meeting Centers
| 5,000
|
FCM State Head
| 10,000
|
FCM ZO Head
| 20,000
|
Exceptions to the above shall be approved by the approving authority as defined in Clause 3.

Grant of Advance:

FCM to consolidate the list of employees on a monthly basis after taking due approvals.

The said list to be shared with the F&A team for effecting transfer of funds.

Responsibilities & Controls:

The designated eligible employee who has been entrusted with the advance shall ensure the following:

Utilize the advance only for official purposes against proper documentation, i.e., receipts, invoices, duly acknowledged by the vendor.

Submitting the claims along with the relevant documents on or before 10th of the following month. The advance will be replenished to the extent of claims approved.

The eligible employees shall restrict the monthly expenditure in petty cash to the extent of the advance granted as per monetary limit as defined under Clause 4 above. Any incremental expenditure shall be incurred only with the prior approval of the approving authority.

All petty cash payments must be made from the money in the petty cash box.

Access to petty cash box should be restricted, with responsibility for the money being clearly assigned. This is to minimize the risk of errors.

Expenses eligible for petty cash advance:

Electricity Charges, Office
Printing & Stationery
Repair & Maintenance
Water Charges
Stamping Charges
Rates & Taxes
Postage & Courier
Telephone & Leased Line
Food & Refreshment Expenses
Housekeeping Service Charges

Capex purchase should not be routed through petty cash expenses.

Procedure for Submission of Claims:

A Petty cash voucher must be submitted for all petty cash claims in Reimbursement System, and it to be approved by the respective immediate supervisor (IS).

All the Petty Cash claims will be reviewed by FCM Team. Any claim without the appropriate documentation will be returned back for re-submission.

Turnaround Time for clearing the vouchers is 3 working days post submission of approved claims to SSC.

Inappropriate use of petty cash:

Petty Cash should not be used for the following:
Borrowing cash from the petty cash.
Paying wages out of petty cash.
Cash expenses exceeding the limit set by the Management.

Policy Violation:

Any employee found to be in violation of this policy may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment. Additionally, any fraudulent or dishonest use of petty cash funds may result in legal action.

Settlement of Petty Cash during Exit:

Any advance lying to the credit of the eligible employee shall be recovered from Full and Final Settlement of the employee by HR operations at the time of exit.

Exception Handling:

Any exceptions to the above policy will require approval of the approving authority as defined in clause 3 above.

The Promotion Policy outlines the guidelines and procedures that govern how employees are considered and selected for advancement within the company. INTRODUCTION

The Company recognizes the value of experienced and talented individuals. The Rehiring Policy outlines the guidelines for rehiring former employees who have left the company voluntarily. This policy aims to provide a fair and consistent approach to re-employment opportunities while considering the needs of the organization.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objectives of the Rehiring policy are:

Tap into the knowledge and skills of former employees who have a proven track record within the organization.
Facilitate a smooth reintegration process for rehired employees.
Ensure that rehiring decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs.

1.2 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Business HR Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.3 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

Eligibility
Cooling Off Period:
Two years from the date of exit of the former employee.
The cooling off period may be less than 2 years only if the employee has consistently received a rating of 4 or above in their previous stint.
Performance and Conduct:
The performance and conduct of former employees will be taken into consideration when evaluating their eligibility for rehiring.
Generally, the rating of last 3 years is considered for the purpose of rehiring.
If the employee had previously received a rating of 2 during their employment tenure in Meridian Finance, the matter will be discussed with the Manager who provided the rating. If the Manager's response is deemed satisfactory, the rehiring offer will be further considered.
If the last appraisal rating of the candidate considered for rehire was 1 then he/she will be ineligible for rehire.

Tenure during their previous stint with Meridian Finance:
The candidate being considered for rehire should have completed at least two years if service with the company in their previous stint or undergone at least two appraisal cycles.

Rehiring Process
Former employees interested in re-employment must follow the standard job application process, including submitting an updated resume or application form.

Rehiring candidates will be required to participate in an interview process to assess their qualifications, skills, and fit for the available position.

When considering rehiring a former employee, their application will be evaluated based on the qualifications and suitability for the specific position, without any guarantee of being hired at the same level or position they held previously. They will be treated on par with other candidates applying for the same position.

Appropriate background checks, such as reference checks and verification of employment history, will be conducted with the HR personnel as part of the rehiring process.

The BHRs also have checklist upon the below following with respect to the candidate considered for rehire and only post just checks, the rehire process is taken forward.

RCU Clearance,
FNF Clearance
RL status

Terms and Conditions of Re-employment

Compensation and Benefits

The compensation and benefits for rehired employees will be determined based on the following factors:
Position offered
The previous salary of the employee in the previous role at Meridian Finance.
Market standards
Peer Parity within Meridian Finance

In case of rehiring from Meridian Group Companies

In case of rehiring an employee from any other group companies, the above terms and conditions holds true. Additionally, a background check and due diligence will be done with the concerned Group entity’s HR Personnel in order to take the offer ahead.

Rehiring Restrictions
Rehired employees may be subject to any non-compete agreements or restrictions they previously agreed to during their initial employment.
Legal restrictions or regulatory requirements may impact the rehiring eligibility of certain individuals.
If the last appraisal rating of the candidate considered for rehire was 1 then he/she will be ineligible for rehire.

Annexure
During the separation process, all employees are assigned a Rehiring tag - Yes/No. This Rehiring tag is also checked during the rehiring process.
If the Rehiring tag is marked as No for an employee who is being rehired, the following steps must be completed then the below approval matrix is applicable:

Grade of the Candidate considered for Hire
| Approving Authority to remove the Rehire tag “NO”
|
Upto Grade OL II & below
| Head BHR
|
OL I & above
| CHRO
|

The Onboarding team will be updating the tag based on the approval received.
After the tag is changed as Yes, the rehiring process is initiated.

INTRODUCTION

The Salary Advance Policy is designed to provide a fair and consistent framework for employees to request and receive salary advances during times of financial need. This policy aims to support employees facing unexpected expenses or financial emergencies while maintaining the financial stability of the organization.

1.1 Policy Objective

The objective of this policy is to provide guidelines for employees to request and receive salary advances in a fair and consistent manner. The policy aims to support employees facing financial emergencies or unexpected expenses while maintaining the financial stability of the organization.

1.2 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s Human Resources Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.3 Policy Amendments and Updates

The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.4 Policy Review and Compliance

Employees and authorized personnel are responsible for complying with this policy.
The Compensation & Benefits team will periodically review the policy to ensure its effectiveness and make any necessary updates or revisions in consultation with relevant stakeholders.

Scope
All regular full-time, are eligible to request a salary advance.
Employees must be in good standing and have no outstanding salary advances or loans from the company.
Employees must also clear the CIBIL check at the time of salary advance.

Request Process
Employees requesting a salary advance must submit a written request through email to their respective BHR with recommendation of their immediate supervisor.
The request should include the reason for the advance, the desired amount, and a proposed repayment plan.
Approval and Disbursement

Approval Process

The immediate supervisor or the respective BHR of the employee will review the request and assess its validity and urgency.
Salary Advance shall only be granted in case of any medical exigency.

Advance Disbursement

If the request is approved, the BHR authorized personnel will determine the maximum advance amount based on the employee's salary.
The employee will be notified of the approved amount.

Permissible amount for salary advance
The maximum permissible amount for a salary advance will be determined by the organization based on the employee's salary and other relevant factors.
The maximum advance amount will typically will not be more than 3 months’ CTC/one year’s CTC of the employee. There is no interest component for salary advance.
The authorized personnel reviewing the salary advance request will assess the employee's financial situation and the purpose of the advance to determine the appropriate amount within the permissible limit.

Repayment
The maximum tenure within which the employee needs to repay the advance amount to the company is 1 year however if the employee exits before one year, then the entire outstanding amount needs to be repaid or adjusted before the last working day of the employee.
Repayment of the salary advance will be deducted from the employee's future salary payments in instalments.
The repayment period will be determined based on the advance amount and the employee's ability to repay without causing financial hardship.
The employee's consent to the repayment terms will be obtained in writing.
If the employee leaves the organization before the full repayment, the outstanding balance will be deducted from the full and final settlement of the employee, subject to applicable laws and regulations

Limitation and Frequency
Salary advances are intended for emergency situations or unexpected expenses and should not be used for regular or discretionary expenses.
The maximum amount of the salary advance will be determined by the organization and may be subject to change based on the employee's salary and other factors.
Employees may request salary advances on a limited basis, typically no more than two times in the entire tenure of their employment with Meridian Finance, to ensure responsible use of this benefit.
The HR Operations Team is responsible to maintain the repository of all such advances being made to the employees.

INTRODUCTION

"My Referrals", is an Employee Referral Program for Meridian Finance, which attempts to reward employees who recommend prospective employees for the organization.

1.1 Policy Objective

The main objective of the “My Referral” Program is to leverage the existing network of employees to attract high-quality candidates who are a good fit for the company culture and values. By tapping into the personal and professional networks of employees, Meridian Finance can potentially find candidates who may not be actively searching for job opportunities but would be interested in joining the organization if referred by someone they know and trust.

1.2 Policy Management

1.2.1 Policy Application and Interpretation

This policy will be in effect from _________.

The Company’s BHR Team will resolve any questions regarding the interpretation and application of this policy. Any exceptions to the Policy will require CHRO’s written approval.

1.2.2 Policy Amendments and Updates
The Company reserves the right to amend this policy at any time. When and where a change in this policy is made the company undertakes to notify the employees as soon as feasible.

1.3 Responsibilities, Compliance

The Company is responsible to specify the types of positions that are eligible for referral and any specific qualifications or requirements for referred candidates.
The Company is responsible to establish a fair and transparent process for submitting referrals, including the use of a designated platform or form.
The employee is responsible to comply with the requirements or procedures outlined in the Employee Referral Program policy.
The employee must maintain confidentiality and professionalism when referring candidates, ensuring that the referral does not create conflicts of interest or bias.
.

Scope and Eligibility
All employees in FL-IV job band and above are eligible (or equivalent job Bands) to refer potential candidates under this program.
However, the following people who can influence the hiring decision are ineligible to benefit from the policy:
Employees in Job Band BL-III and above (or equivalent Grade)
Members of the Human Resources Department
Employees referring immediate family members to the Company.
Hiring manager or anyone specific who is involved in the selection process for a specific position.

Referral Reward
For a candidate hired through the referral program, due recognition will be given to the concerned employee. This will be in the form of Referral Reward given to the concerned employee in two instalments post joining of the referred candidate.
First Instalment, On completion of 30 days of the referred employee’s employment in the organisation
Second Instalment- On completion of 120 days of the referred employee’s employment in the organisation
Please refer Annexure, 1 for the referral amounts and the instalments defined as per grades.

General Policy Guidelines
All job postings open under the My Referral program can be accessed through My Referral portal on the HR portal.
Path to access the same in the HR portal:

the HR portal login >> Talent Acquisition >> Current Job openings

In cases where the same candidate is referred from two or more sources, the source from where his/her resume was received first as determined by the date and time stamp on the email sent will be considered valid and payments will be made accordingly. HR Team keeps a track of all resumes received along with date of receipt to ensure correct source is mapped to each resume.
During the pay-out of the Reward both the referrer and referee should be on active employment. In case either of them is serving notice period or has exited from the organization the referrer will not be eligible for the pay-out.
Referral Reward will be paid along with the Salary payment and applicable taxes therein will be borne by the employee.
Claw back Period: If the employee hired through referral leaves the Organization within six months from the date of joining, then the referral reward will be forfeited from the referrer.

policies.title: Dress Code Policy
policies.content:
Dress Code Policy

Policy Title: Dress Code Policy
Applicability: Applicable to all employees of Meridian Finance and all registered legal entities under the umbrella.
Prepared by: Team, Human Resources
Reviewed by: Head, Human Resources
Approved by: Chief Human Resources Officer

1. Purpose
This policy sets out the standard of dress and grooming expected of employees, so that everyone presents a professional and consistent image to customers, partners, and colleagues. As a financial services organisation, the way we present ourselves reflects the trust our customers place in us.

2. Scope
This policy applies to all employees, including full time employees, employees on probation, trainees, and contractual staff, across all offices and branches.

3. General Guidelines
Employees are expected to be dressed in a clean, well groomed, and professional manner during working hours. Attire should be appropriate to the role, the location, and any customer or external interaction planned for the day.

4. Business Formal
Business formal attire is expected on days with customer meetings, external visitors, audits, or leadership reviews.
For men: formal full sleeve shirts, formal trousers, formal shoes, and where required a tie or blazer.
For women: formal shirts or blouses with formal trousers, formal skirts of appropriate length, or formal Indian wear such as sarees or salwar suits, with formal footwear.

5. Business Casual
On regular working days without external interaction, business casual attire is acceptable.
For men: collared shirts or polo shirts, chinos or formal trousers, and closed shoes.
For women: smart tops with trousers, or formal Indian wear, with closed or formal footwear.

6. Casual Fridays
Employees may dress in smart casuals on Fridays, subject to any team specific requirements. Smart casuals should still be neat and presentable. Denims that are clean and without tears are permitted on Fridays.

7. What is not permitted
The following are not considered appropriate for the workplace on any working day: shorts, three fourth trousers, sleeveless or spaghetti tops, tank tops, torn or heavily distressed denims, slippers or flip flops, sportswear and gym wear, and any clothing with offensive or political slogans or graphics.

8. Grooming and hygiene
Employees are expected to maintain personal hygiene and grooming. Identity cards must be worn and kept visible at all times within office premises.

9. Special situations
On days declared as ethnic days or theme days by the organisation, employees may dress accordingly. Employees with a medical or religious requirement that affects their attire may reach out to the HR helpdesk for reasonable accommodation.

10. Non compliance
Repeated non compliance with the dress code may be addressed by the reporting manager or HR. In persistent cases it may be treated under the Disciplinary Action Policy.

For any clarification on this policy, employees may contact the HR helpdesk.
